product_system: 3.0T HD CTL Array (8-Channel); 3.0T HD CTL Array, A/B Port
title: Cable routing to prevent heating
body:
1. Route cables through the center of the magnet bore.
2. Place cables under the cushion whenever possible.
3. Keep the length of the cable in the bore to a minimum.
4. When possible, avoid bending the cable 180 degrees.
5. Route cables out of the bore in the most direct way possible, without looping or coiling.
Note: Routing cable near the sides of the bore increases the likelihood of cable heating from induced currents.
anchor: Route cables through the center of the magnet bore. Routing cable near the sides of the bore increases the likelihood of cable heating from induced currents. Place cables under the cushion whenever possible.

doc_title: Operator Manual for the 3.0T HD CTL Array
product_system: 3.0T HD CTL Array (8-Channel); 3.0T HD CTL Array, A/B Port
title: Coil Cleaning and Disinfection
body: Clean and disinfect the Coil after removing from packaging prior to first use. Cleaning and disinfection of patient contact surfaces is recommended following each use. Clean with commercially available wipes containing 0.525% minimum sodium hypochlorite as the only active ingredient, or use a lint free cloth saturated with 1:10 dilution of bleach (minimum 5.25% sodium hypochlorite), or use a lint free cloth saturated with 70% isopropyl alcohol solution. Inspect to ensure visual cleanliness prior to disinfection. Repeat cleaning until all visible soil has been removed. Disinfect with commercially available wipes containing 0.525% minimum sodium hypochlorite or a lint free cloth and 1:10 bleach dilution. For general disinfection or disinfection following cleaning of blood and/or body fluids, 5 minutes contact time is recommended. After cleaning and disinfecting with bleach, wipe surfaces with a disposable lint free wipe dampened with purified water to remove any remaining bleach residue and allow device to air dry indoors before use.

title: Unified Phantom Data Collection Procedure
body: 1. Place the coil on the patient table and latch it to the table. 2. Place the TL unified phantoms on the center of the TL section of the coil. 3. Align the phantoms to the center in S/I and R/L directions. 4. Place the large cylindrical unified phantom on the CT section. 5. Adjust the large cylindrical unified phantom such that it is in complete contact with the TL unified phantom. 6. Adjust TL unified phantoms such that both the phantoms are in complete contact with each other. 7. Connect the coil to respective port of the system LPCA. 8. Landmark the coil on the mark and advance to scan. 9. Refer to Section 3-2-2-3 of this document to run scan with the Unified Phantom Set.

From the Common Service Desktop (CSD) select {Image Quality], Multi-Coil QA Tool and Click here to start this tool. The Coil Log Viewer will open. 3. The current coil field will be automatically filled in, based on the Coil ID of the coil connected to the LPCA. 4. Enter the Coil Serial # into the provided field. 5. From the MCQA Tool GUI, press the [Start] button to begin the test. 6. A warning dialog will be shown, asking the user to verify the coil/phantom set-up and position. Ensure the phantom and coil setup is proper and select [Yes] to continue. 7. Once the test has completed, the name of the Results file will be listed, along with the Pass/Fail status of the test. 8. Record the Measured ISNR and the LSL for each channel displayed in the Status Window on a separate sheet.

title: Troubleshooting - Coil Fault or Not Recognized
body:
Symptom: The system reports a coil fault during prescan or does not recognize the coil connection to the system when selected in the software.

Probable Cause 1: The coil connector has become disconnected from the system interface.
Suggested Actions: Check to make sure the coil connector is fully engaged.
Resolution: Engage connector and try the scan again.

Probable Cause 2: There is a DC short or open somewhere within the DC path inside the coil.
Suggested Actions: Perform Section 3-3, External Cable Check.
Resolution: If there is no cable damage detected, replace the coil.

Probable Cause 3: The output cable has a short or an open.
Suggested Actions: Perform Section 3-3, External Cable Check, to confirm.
Resolution: Replace the coil cable assembly.

Probable Cause 4: There is a problem with the DC bias from the system interface.
Suggested Actions: Check to ensure the correct DC bias is being provided to the coil during transmit and receive per GE MRI System Service Manual. Try a similar 8-channel coil to see if the same problem occurs.
Resolution: Correct MRI system problem.

Probable Cause 5: Coil ID issues.
Suggested Actions: From CSD, select Diagnostics, Manual Tests, SRI Functional Checks, and run the SRI Coil ID test. Compare the coil ID value found to that listed in the coil configuration.
Resolution: If the value does not match, or no coil ID is found, replace the cable assembly.
anchor: Symptom #1: The system reports a coil fault during prescan or does not recognize the coil connection to the system when selected in the software.

title: External Cable Replacement
body: 1. Remove coil bottom cover by removing all screws around the perimeter and down the center of the base. 2. Remove the cable clamp that holds down the cable assembly (see Figure 29). 3. Disconnect the SMB plugs and DC plug on the cable end from the interface boards. 4. Remove the old cable assembly. 5. Attach the new cable assembly (see Figure 30) to the coil and make sure the cable strain relief matches the notch of the former (see Figure 31). The side of the cable connector with the "do not" label should face up (see Figure 31). If it doesn't face up, rotate the strain relief. Make sure that the cable clamp holds the cable jacket, and then tighten the cable clamp with the screws. Connect all eight SMB plugs and the DC Plug to the corresponding receptacles on the interface board. The receptacles are marked CH1-8 to correspond with the labels on the cables. Do not route RF cables and DC wires above the bosses shown in Figure 29 because the corresponding bosses on the bottom cover will squeeze the cables and DC wires when the bottom cover is closed. 6. Reattach the coil bottom cover.
anchor: Connect all eight SMB plugs and the DC Plug to the corresponding receptacles on the interface board. The receptacles are marked CH1-8 to correspond with the labels on the cables.

doc_title: Operator Manual for the 1.5T CTL Coil
product_system: 1.5T CTL Coil (4 Channel / 8 Channel)
title: Cable routing and patient safety during scanning
body: Route cables through the center of the magnet bore. Routing cable near the sides of the bore increases the likelihood of cable heating from induced currents. Place cables under the cushion whenever possible. Keep the length of the cable in the bore to a minimum. When possible, avoid bending the cable 180 degrees. Route cables out of the bore in the most direct way possible, without looping or coiling. Monitor the patient periodically. If the patient reports heating, burning or tingling sensations, stop the scan immediately.
anchor: Route cables through the center of the magnet bore. Routing cable near the sides of the bore increases the likelihood of cable heating

title: Patient burn risk – cable positioning
body: Do not cross or loop coil cables. Do not loop RF receive coil cables and ECG leads. Do not allow the coil cable to come into contact with the skin of the patient. Use a thermal resistant material or pad to keep the cable from touching the patient. Failure to do so may result in patient burns.

product_system: 1.5T CTL Coil (4 Channel / 8 Channel)
title: RF heating at adjacent body parts
body: RF can cause localized heating at contact points between adjacent body parts when a loop is formed. Such localized heating can result in a tingling sensation, discomfort, or burns. This could occur when a patient's hands are touching or when a female patient's breasts are compressed to her chest. Use pads between body parts to avoid creating a loop with adjacent body parts.
anchor: RF can cause localized heating at contact points between adjacent body parts when a loop is formed.

body: Do not use accessories (e.g. pads or straps) that have not been specifically tested and approved for use in the MR environment. Use only GE recommended accessories. Use of non-approved accessories may result in patient burns or injuries or image degradation. Even auxiliary devices labeled as compatible with MR equipment are capable of causing injury if the manufacturer's instructions are not followed.

doc_title: Operator Manual for the 1.5T CTL Coil
product_system: 1.5T CTL Coil (4 Channel / 8 Channel)
title: Head-First Imaging Patient Positioning
body: 1. Remove the cervical bridge of the coil. Press both release buttons simultaneously to remove the bridge. 2. For best image quality, the cervical bridge should be used. However, if patient size does not allow for use of the cervical bridge, attach the adapter block to the coil. 3. Position the patient head first, supine, with the top of the shoulders resting firmly against the coil sides. Use earpads to secure the patient's head in the coil. Position the patient's arms to his or her sides. A cotton sheet should be used as necessary to keep the patient's skin from touching the coil. 4. Align the cervical bridge with the alignment pegs and press the bridge onto the posterior section of the coil. 5. Plug the coil cable into the appropriately labeled port of the system receptacle. The coil connector and cable should always be routed directly to the magnet and should not form loops. 6. Localize the anatomy and advance to scan.
anchor: Position the patient head first, supine, with the top of the shoulders resting firmly against the coil sides.

title: SNR Setup for 11.0 M3A and Greater with Unified Phantom Set
body: 1. Place the coil on the patient table and latch it to the table. 2. Place the TL unified phantoms on the centre of the TL section of the coil. 3. Align the phantoms to the centre in S/I and R/L directions. 4. Place the large cylindrical unified phantom on the CT section and fix the C-Spine Bridge to the hooks provided. 5. Adjust the large cylindrical unified phantom such that it is in complete contact with the TL unified phantom. 6. Adjust TL unified phantoms such that both the phantoms are in complete contact with each other. 7. Connect the coil to respective port of the system LPCA. 8. Landmark the coil at the cross mark line on the C-Spine Bridge and advance to scan.

title: SNR Measurement Method
body: The image quality check uses two consecutive acquisitions for the same slice. The signal is measured at the center of the phantom with a ROI of about 60% of the phantom size. The noise is measured on the subtracted image of the two consecutive signal images using the same ROI. SNR is calculated by dividing the Signal mean by the noise standard deviation. All measurements are performed on composite images.

doc_title: Service Manual, GE Signa 1.5T 8-Channel CTL Coil
product_system: GE Signa 1.5T 8-Channel CTL Coil
title: Troubleshooting Coil Fault or Unrecognized Connection
body: Symptom #1: The system reports a coil fault during prescan or does not recognize the coil connection to the system when selected in the software. Coil connector disconnected: Engage connector and try the scan again. Make sure the indicator light on the patient table turns green with the proper coil selected on the console. One or more PIN diodes failed: From inside the coil, check the PIN diodes using a DVM. Use diode mode for forward-bias measurements and resistance mode for reverse-bias measurements. Note that there should be no reverse-bias leakage. Bad PIN diodes are usually shorted or exhibit reverse-bias leakage current. Replace the coil. DC short or open inside coil: Check the coil and associated DC paths with a DVM, in both diode check and resistance modes. If a short or open is observed, check the output cable by itself. If the cable and PIN diodes are okay, then replace the coil. Output cable short or open: Disconnect the cable at the coil and check each coaxial line with a DVM (resistance). Try moving and twisting the cable as you watch the meter to find any intermittent connections. Inspect the center pins of the SMB and Bendix connections for wear and proper engagement into the mating connection. Replace the cable. DC bias or coil ID problem: Check to ensure the correct DC bias is being provided to the coil during transmit and receive per GEMS System Service Manual. Try a similar 2-channel coil to see if the same problem occurs. Correct MRI system problem. Coil ID mismatch: Start the diagnostic by selecting SRI Coil ID and Run. The diagnostic will display the contents of the coil ID chip whenever the connector is inserted. Follow the troubleshooting instructions if the correct ID is not displayed. When the troubleshooting is complete and the ID is still not displayed, replace the cable.
anchor: The system reports a coil fault during prescan or does not recognize the coil connection to the system when selected in the software.

doc_title: Service Manual, GE Signa 1.5T 8-Channel CTL Coil
product_system: GE Signa 1.5T 8-Channel CTL Coil
title: Troubleshooting Poor SNR or Image Quality
body: Symptom #2: The coil does not pass SNR tests or exhibits poor image quality on patient scans. High noise level in one or more channels: Look at the uncombined images to determine which channel has the problem. Compare the noise standard deviation measurements between channels and system performance logs; they should be approximately the same. Replace the coil. Low signal in one or more channels: Look at the uncombined images to determine which channel has the problem. Compare signal mean measurements between channels and system performance logs. Replace the coil. Excessive ghosting: Window and level the images down to look at the background for signs of ghosting. Try padding the phantom in the holder. Try running the scan without the phantom holder to see if the ghosting diminishes. Try turning off the cold heads to see if the ghosting is vibration-related. If padding or changing the phantom position can minimize ghosting, then the problem is caused by excessive vibration elsewhere in the system. If the ghosting is not symptomatic of phantom positioning or padding, then replace the coil. DC bias problem: Check to ensure the correct DC bias is being provided to the coils during transmit and receive per GEMS System Service Manual. Correct MRI system DC bias problem.
anchor: The coil does not pass SNR tests or exhibits poor image quality on patient scans.

title: Fat Saturation Technique - Patient Positioning
body: For best fat saturation results: 1. Position the patient as close to isocenter as possible. 2. Ensure that the non-imaged foot is away from the coil to avoid phase overlapping. 3. For axial imaging, use an axial positioner. 4. Before specifying the slices, use the same FOV you intend to use in your study for positioning or use explicit positioning. Note: Off-center FOV imaging is more complex and difficult. Imaging at the edge of the magnet may produce poor fat saturation. Use of graphic indication from a large FOV positioner sometimes results in software error, producing blank slices, shifted slices, or both.
anchor: For best fat saturation results, position the patient as close to isocenter as possible, while ensuring that the non-imaged foot is away from the coil to avoid phase overlapping.

product_system: 1.5T 8ch T/R Knee Coil (RF Tech)
title: Troubleshooting No Signal from Knee Coil
body: Problem: Unable to pre-scan or receiving no signal when scanning. Steps: 1. Verify appropriate system coil selection (refer to Operators Manual). 2. Verify landmark is correct and cradle has not unlatched. 3. Verify scan locations and FOV offsets are correct. 4. Perform continuity check on external cable (must be performed by GE authorized Service Engineer). 5. Verify coil is properly positioned. 6. If still no signal, scan (transmit and receive) with body coil. Remove imaging coil from magnet bore before scanning with body coil. If no signal with body coil, problem likely with MR system. If body coil scan successful, problem likely with coil. Contact GE for further assistance.
anchor: Verify that you have made the appropriate system coil selection. Refer to the Operators Manual for additional information.

product_system: 1.5T 8ch T/R Knee Coil (RF Tech)
title: Troubleshooting Poor Image Quality
body: Problem: Image quality not as expected. Steps: 1. Review selected protocol. For Periodic Quality Assurance, ensure protocol identical to Systems Recommended Protocols. For diagnostic images, may need to increase NEX or FOV. 2. Perform continuity check on external cable (must be performed by GE authorized Service Engineer). 3. Verify no loops in cables. 4. Verify no metal or ferromagnetic objects close to coil, patient or magnet (i.e., safety pin, hair pin). 5. Verify coil properly positioned. 6. Verify center frequency within frequency adjustment range for system. 7. Verify R1, R2 and TG values from pre-scan within normally expected ranges. 8. Perform MCQA (Multi Coil Quality Assurance) Test. If values outside normal parameters, perform phantom scan with coil. Remove imaging coil from magnet bore before scanning with body coil. If same problems with body coil, likely MR system problem. If body coil scan satisfactory, acquire scan using another coil of same type plugged into same system port. If image quality visibly improved, may be coil problem. Contact GE for further assistance.
anchor: Review the selected protocol. If you are performing the Periodic Quality Assurance, be sure your protocol is identical to the protocol provided in your Systems Recommended Protocols.

product_system: 1.5T 8ch T/R Knee Coil (RF Tech)
title: Knee Coil Cable Replacement
body:
Personnel: 1 person; Time: 30 mins procedure (0 min preliminary, 0 min finalization).
1. Remove all screws on the upper coil cable port cover and remove the coil cover.
2. Remove the four brass screws that hold down the cable clamps (see illustration 7-1).
3. Disconnect the cable by grasping the coil connector housing, and pulling the cable away from the coil connector in a downward direction (see illustration 7-2).
4. Remove the old cable assembly.
5. Fix a new cable assembly on the T/R knee coil and reattach the cable lock with four brass screws.
6. Connect the coil connector housing to the corresponding receptacles on the interfaces board.
7. Close the coil cover lock with 4 RENY screws.
8. Perform MCQA after replacement.
anchor: Remove the four brass screws that hold down the cable clamps(see illustration 7-1).

doc_title: 1.5T HNS Coil Installation (Direction 24239893TPH)
product_system: 1.5T HNS Coil
title: 1.5T HNS Coil Configuration Procedure
body: 1. Go to the scan desktop and select the [New Patient] button. 2. Assemble the coil in one of the 5 valid hardware setup configurations and make sure the coil components have a snug fit with each other. Setup 1: Posterior Head Component + Face Component. Setup 2: Posterior Head Component + Face Component + TL Component. Setup 3: Posterior Head Component + Horseshoe Component + TL Component. Setup 4: Chest Component Added To Setup 3. Setup 5: Posterior Head Component + Face Component + TL Component + Neck Component. 3. Plug the connector, from the Head Neck Unit (HNU) of the coil, into the appropriate Port connector on the LPCA Port. If the coil is not configured on the system a pop-up box will appear. If the box does not appear, then proceed to step 5. 4. Select [Yes] to configure the new coil. If the process is successful a pop-up message will be displayed. Continue the process of plugging in each of the five coil set-ups per illustrations 1-5. 5. Prescribe a new exam and enter patient information. 6. Click on the coil selection button and verify that the HNS coil is present under currently connected on the scanner user interface. When the five coil Setups have been configured, you will see all the coil entries in the Coil Names window. 7. After successfully configuring the coil proceed to Section 5, HNS Coil MCQA Setup.
anchor: Assemble the coil in one of the 5 valid hardware setup configurations below and make sure the coil components have a snug fit with each other.

doc_title: 1.5T Head Neck Spine (HNS) Service Methods
product_system: 1.5T Head Neck Spine (HNS) Coil
title: Receiving No Signal Troubleshooting
body: 1. If Neck Chest unit is used, ensure connector is fully engaged to receptacle on posterior Head Neck unit. 2. Verify landmark is correct and cradle has not unlatched. 3. Verify scan locations and any FOV offsets are correct. 4. Perform continuity check on output cable (Section 1.5.4) if you lose some signals from some coil channels (must be performed by GE authorized Service Engineer). 5. Verify coil is positioned with cable exiting towards the bore. 6. If still no signal, try to scan (transmit and receive) with body coil. Remove imaging coil from magnet bore before scanning with body coil. If no signal with body coil, problem probably lies with MR system. If body coil scan completes successfully, there is probably a problem with Brain Spine coil.
anchor: Perform a continuity check on the output cable (Section 1.5.4) if you lose some signals from some of coil channels. The continuity check must be performed by a GE authorized Service Engineer.

doc_title: 1.5T Head Neck Spine (HNS) Service Methods
product_system: 1.5T Head Neck Spine (HNS) Coil
title: Image Quality Troubleshooting
body: 1. Perform a continuity check on output cable (Section 1.5.4). Must be performed by GE authorized Service Engineer. 2. Verify there are no loops in cables. 3. Verify there are no metal or ferromagnetic objects close to coil, patient or magnet (i.e., safety pin, hair pin). 4. Verify coil is properly positioned. 5. Verify center frequency is within frequency adjustment range for your system. 6. Verify R1, R2 and TG values from pre-scan are within normally expected ranges. 7. Perform system Quality Assurance MCQA test. If values do not fall within normal operating parameters, perform phantom scan with body coil. Remove imaging coil from magnet bore before scanning with body coil. If body coil scan is satisfactory, acquire scan using another coil of same type (receive-only, phased array or transmit/receive) and same system coil selection.
anchor: Verify that the R1, R2 and TG values from the pre-scan are within normally expected ranges.

product_system: 1.5T Head Neck Spine (HNS) Coil
title: Artifacts Troubleshooting (Black Line, Strip Lines, Signal Void)
body: 1. Verify there is no metal present in area being scanned in or on patient. 2. Verify no hair is caught trapped in connectors between anterior and posterior sections of Head Neck unit. This may appear as intermittent oscillations. 3. Verify cable connector of Neck Chest unit is fully plugged into receptacle on posterior section of Head Neck unit. If connector is not fully plugged in, there may be a coil not present error or there may be intermittent oscillations. 4. If you have oscillation of preamp you will see striped lines.
anchor: Verify that no hair is caught trapped in the connectors between the anterior and posterior sections of the Head Neck unit.

If there are any broken, deformed or recessed pins or coaxial connectors, replace cable assembly. When you replace cable assembly, you need to make sure the configuration of jumpers on interface board for upgrade and forward production systems. Remove cable assembly from coil. See Chapter 5, 1.5T HNS Coil Cable Replacement.

title: RF Signal Channels Check
body: 1. Disconnect the coil cable. 2. Use a multimeter to assure no open circuit condition exists between the RF ground shields of the RF coax connector in the system side and the coils side (Refer to Table 3-1 or Table 3-2). 3. Use the multimeter to assure an open circuit condition exists between the center pin and the shield for each RF connector in the coil side. 4. If one or more of the readings indicate a short, replace the cable. 5. If all readings indicate an open circuit condition, proceed to the DC Lines Continuity Check.

doc_title: 1.5T Head Neck Spine (HNS) Service Methods
product_system: 1.5T Head Neck Spine (HNS) Coil
title: HNS Rev. 2 Cable Replacement
body: 1. Put an ESD wrist strap on and ground. 2. Unscrew the bottom cover and remove from coil. Retain the original screws used. 3. Unscrew the cable clamp from the coil. Retain the original screws used. 4. Identify and remove RF connectors (CH in Head Neck Unit (HNU), J in Thoracic Lumbar Unit (TLU)) from interface Board. Pliers may be necessary for removal of the MMCX connectors. 5. Identify and remove DC connectors (DC) from Interface Board and Coil ID PCB. 6. Remove the system cable (with or without the coil id). 7. If the cable FRU is with the coil id, remove the coil ID PCB from Interface Board. If the cable FRU exists without the coil id board, then remove only the cable. 8. Identify the Interface Board Assembly and the coil ID PCB located on the Interface Board (Head Neck Unit (HNU) Only). Carefully remove the Coil ID assembly. 9. Install the new system cable. 10. Align the cable clamp of the cable into the notch of former slot. Screw down cable clamp using original screws.
anchor: Unscrew the bottom cover and remove from coil. Retain the original screws used.

title: 1.5T HNS Mirror Assembly Inspection and Repair
body: 1. Inspect mirrors to ensure that they are not coming loose from the plastic housings. If the mirrors are coming loose a new mirror assembly will be needed. 2. Inspect all parts for broken snap features. If any of the snap features are broken, a new mirror assembly will be needed. a. There are 2 located on each end of each of the cross pieces (the locking bar, the rotating mirror, and the fixed mirror). b. There are 5 on each of the side covers. c. There are 3 on each of the top rails. 3. If any of the cross pieces have been dislocated from their proper position, the side covers will need to be removed to properly re-seat the snap feature. This is due to the locking features on the inside of the side covers.
anchor: Inspect mirrors to ensure that they are not coming loose from the plastic housings. If the mirrors are coming loose a new mirror assembly will be needed.

title: Coil Storage Procedure
body: 1. Store coil in air conditioned area with environmental conditions within GE recommended MR suite conditions. 2. Place coil in horizontal position similar to orientation on MRI table. 3. title: Applied Parts and Patient Contact Requirements
body: All surface areas of the TLU and HNU (with Anterior Unit or Adapter Block), except the bottom surface that sits on the patient table, are considered applied parts and may come into direct contact with the patient. All surface areas of the NCU are considered applied parts and may come into direct contact with the patient. Pads and/or thermal-resistant materials should be used to prevent the coil surfaces from touching the patient. Pads and/or thermal-resistant material must be used to ensure the patient cannot touch the coil cables and connectors.

title: Cable Routing Safety
body: Route cables through the center of the magnet bore. Place cables under the cushion whenever possible. Routing near the sides of the bore increases the likelihood of cable heating from induced currents. Keep the length of the cable in the bore to a minimum. When possible, avoid bending the cable 180 degrees. Route cables out of the bore in the most direct way possible, without looping or coiling.

title: Patient Burn Prevention - Body Loop Formation
body: RF can cause localized heating at contact points between adjacent body parts when a loop is formed. Loops may be formed by clasped hands, crossed arms, legs or feet, when a patient's hands are touching another body part, or when a female patient's breasts are compressed to her chest. Use pads between body parts to avoid creating a loop with adjacent body parts.

title: Reporting of Serious Incidents
body:
Report any serious incident related to the use of this GE Healthcare device to both the manufacturer and the health authority/competent authority where the device is installed.

To report to GE Healthcare:
- Either contact your local service representative
- Or report to: In-box.complaints@gehealthcare.com

Provide the following information:
- The catalogue number or the model designation of the device as stated on its identification plate affixed on the device
- The SystemID/serial number/lot number of the device
- Date of incident
- Description of incident, including any patient or user impact/injury
- Your contact information (facility, address, contact name, title, and telephone number)

title: Reporting of Incidents with the Coil - Smoke, Sparks, or Loud Noise
body:
In the unlikely event that a coil creates smoke, sparks or makes an unusually loud noise:
1. Contact your local service representative to report the incident.
2. Do not use the coil until a GE Service Representative inspects the coil and indicates it is safe to use.

Users should immediately report to GE any incidents or injuries that result from coil operation involving a patient, operator, or maintenance employee.

If an accident occurs as a result of coil operation, do not operate the equipment until an authorized investigation has been conducted.

doc_title: Operator Manual for the 1.5T HD Head, Neck, and Spine Array and the 3.0T Head, Neck, and Spine Array Coils
product_system: 1.5T HD Head, Neck, and Spine Array; 3.0T Head, Neck, and Spine Array
title: Installing the Mirror onto the HNU Anterior Unit
body:
1. If the mirror has come off and top rails are still attached to the mirror, push the locking bar on the mirror into the up position. This will release the top rails from the mirror.
2. Attach the top rails onto the bottom rails that are screwed onto the anterior unit.
3. Insert the front tab on the top right rail into the front cut-out of the bottom rail.
4. Gently push the top rail down onto the bottom rail. A click will be heard when the top rail is secured to the bottom rail.
5. If needed, attach the opposite rail using the same method as described in steps 3 and 4.
6. Push the locking bar of the mirror into the up position.
7. Align the channels at the bottom of the left and right side of the mirror with the channel of the left and right rails.
8. Slide the mirror onto the rails. The mirror needs to slide past the rail tabs.
9. Gently push the locking bar on the mirror down to lock the mirror in place.
10. The mirror is now installed onto the anterior unit.
section: Installing the mirror onto the HNU Anterior (Face) Unit
anchor: push the locking bar on the mirror into the up position (shown in figure 3-9). This will release the top rails from the mirror

title: HNS Coil Components and Element Groups
body:
The HNS Coil consists of five components:
A = TL Spine (TL) (groups 3 through 6)
B = HNU Posterior Unit (Posterior Head and groups 1 and 2)
C = HNU Anterior Unit (Face)
D = Anterior Adapter Block (Horseshoe)
E = Neck Chest Unit (Chest)
Element groups are marked 1-6 on the sides of the coil for positioning and landmarking. The TL component may be used independently.
anchor: A = TL Spine (TL) (groups 3 through 6) B = HNU Posterior Unit (Posterior Head and groups 1 and 2) C = HNU Anterior Unit (Face)

title: Connector Cover Required When Not Using Chest Component
body: When scanning patients without the chest component, always place the connector cover securely over the connector on the Posterior Head Component. The cover prevents the patient's hand from coming in contact with the connector. Failure to comply will leave the connector exposed, placing the patient at risk for RF burns or shock if the patient touches the connector during a scan.

title: Selecting Proper Coil Configuration for Study
body:

title: Coil and patient positioning steps
body: 1. Place the TL Spine component on the table, then place the pad on it. Patient will enter the scanner head first, so be sure cables extend toward the docking end of the table. 2. Place the Posterior Head component on the table as shown, making sure it clears the cradle docking mechanism. Interlock the pegs on the bottom with the holes in the TL Spine Component. Place pad on the Posterior Head component. Ensure that the TL cable lies within the cable channel beneath the Posterior Head component. When placed properly, the Posterior Head component will sit evenly on top of the TL cable. 3. Position the patient in the supine position on the table and lower the head into the Posterior Head component. Make sure that shoulders touch the shoulder rest area. 4. Place the Face component over the Posterior Head component. Secure Face component with the blue latches on both sides. Ensure that no hair or fabric is caught between the components.

doc_title: Operator Manual for the 1.5T HD Head, Neck, and Spine Array and the 3.0T Head, Neck, and Spine Array Coils
product_system: 1.5T HD Head, Neck, and Spine Array; 3.0T Head, Neck, and Spine Array
title: Cleaning and Disinfection of HNS Coils and Accessories
body:
1. Clean with commercially available wipes containing 0.525% minimum sodium hypochlorite as the only active ingredient. If not available, use one of these methods:
   a. Lint-free cloth saturated with 1:10 dilution of bleach (minimum 5.25% sodium hypochlorite) diluted with tap water, OR
   b. Lint-free cloth saturated with 70% isopropyl alcohol solution (100% isopropyl alcohol and 30% tap water), OR
   c. Lint-free cloth with commercially prepared 70% concentration isopropyl alcohol.
2. Carefully clean all surfaces including cracks and crevices. Place a wipe around a rigid implement (GE Part Number 5878912 or equivalent) to get into cracks. Use swabs covered with wipes or diluted cleaning agents for blind holes and recessed areas.
3. Inspect to ensure visual cleanliness prior to disinfection. Repeat cleaning until all visible soil is removed.
4. Disinfect with commercially available wipes containing 0.525% minimum sodium hypochlorite following manufacturer's instructions. If not available, disinfect with lint-free cloth and 1:10 dilution of bleach (minimum 5.25% sodium hypochlorite) diluted with tap water.
5. For general disinfection or disinfection following cleaning of blood and/or body fluids, 5 minutes contact time is recommended.
6. After cleaning and disinfecting with bleach, wipe surfaces with disposable lint-free wipe dampened with purified water to remove bleach residue and allow device to air dry indoors before use.
7. Dispose of materials according to all federal, state, and local regulations.
section: Cleaning and Disinfection Recommendations for the MR System, Coils and Most Accessories
anchor: Clean with commercially available wipes that contain 0.525% minimum sodium hypochlorite as the only active ingredient.

doc_title: 3.0T Head, Neck, Spine Coil Service Manual
product_system: 3.0T Head, Neck, Spine Coil (P/N 5367722)
title: 3T HNS Coil Installation Procedure for HDx Systems
body: 1. Ensure latest software build is loaded; minimum is 15.0_M3 or 15.0_M4 (not applicable to 15.0_M4A). 2. Open Config File Manager (CFM) from [Utilities] tab of MR CSD. 3. Go to Coil config section and remove HNS configurations: For FP system with M3 or M4 software, remove 5 configurations: <GE_HNSTLsNoUse>, <GE_HNSCTL2>, <GE_HNSBrPlCsII>, <GE_HNSCTBrain2>, <GE_HNS NVfullFP>. For Upgrade system, remove 6 configurations: <GE_HNSTLsNoUse>, <GE_HNSCTBrain2>, <GE_HNSBPCsII4>, <GE_HNSBPCsII3>, <GE_HNSCsICTs0>, <GE_HNSBPCsII1>. Remove by: a. Select coil from coil name, b. Select Remove Coil, c. Select Yes, d. Repeat for all coils, e. Select Save Changes then Yes, f. Select Quit. 4. Insert Coil CD (PN 5325975) into DVD Drive. 5. Open command window and type: su, <root password>, mount /mnt/cdrom, /mnt/cdrom/coil_prescan_update. 6. Launch CSD, go to [Utilities], Select [Install Coil CD]. 7. Select [Click here to start this tool]; if already installed, eject CD and proceed to step 8; may take up to 10 minutes; message should state 'Coil Media Installation Successful', remove CD and close xterm window. 8. Reboot System and login as SDC. 9. Connect coil to LPCA as shown in Setup 1; pop-up will state 'A new coil has been connected to the system, Do you want to configure?', Select YES then OK. 10. After configuration of setup 1, remove coil cable from LPCA before changing to setup 2. 11. Repeat steps 9 and 10 for setups 2 through 4.
section: 2.1 3T HNS Coil Installation Procedure for HDx systems
anchor: Make sure that the latest software build is loaded on the system prior to installing the HNS coil. The minimum software build is 15.0_M3 or 15.0_M4.

title: 3T HNS Coil MCQA Test Configuration Requirements
body: The coils must be tested in 3 configurations: 1. The TL unit only. 2. Posterior + NCU + Horseshoe Adapter + TL. 3. Posterior + Anterior. This is done to ensure modularity in design and in diagnostics. The MCQA tool can ONLY run on the above mentioned individual coil configurations. The MCQA tool can NOT run on all coil configurations at the same time. MCQA will not run and will report that the configuration is invalid if an attempt is made to scan with an unsupported combination of coils.

title: 3.0T HNS Posterior Head Face Coil-Phantom Setup
body:
1. Place Posterior Head Face section on the table.
2. Place the 3.0T HNS phantom positioner in the coil. Place the Legacy cylinder phantom into the phantom positioner.
3. Carefully align the face component part of the coil with the connector pins over the Posterior head face section and latch both the coil sections into place. (The scanner will not operate if the coil sections are not latched correctly).
4. Connect the appropriate cables to the LPCA.
5. Landmark the coil at the inferior edge of the arch. Press advance to scan.
6. Refer to Section 3.10 to run the MCQA Tool with the Legacy Phantom Set.

body:

2. Place the phantom positioner in the Head section.
3. Place and latch the Horseshoe on the Head section.

6. Connect the chest part to the posterior Head section and complete the setup.
7. Ensure that the two TL bricks are in contact with each other and ensure the superior TL brick is in contact with the phantom positioner.

doc_title: 3.0T Head, Neck, Spine Coil Service Manual
product_system: 3.0T Head, Neck, Spine Coil (P/N 5367722)
title: Run MCQA on 3.0T Head, Neck, Spine Coil
body:
1. From Common Service Desktop (CSD) go to Service Browser and select [Image Quality], "Multi-Coil QA Tool" and then "Click here to start this tool".
2. Upon start-up, the coil that is connected to the system gets selected in the Current coil field.
3. A pop-up displays requesting you to select correct Phantom Set. Press OK.
4. If a Legacy Phantom Set is being used, select "Legacy (Old Phantom)" from the dropdown menu next to the Phantom Set field. If "Unified Phantom Set" is being used then select "Unified Phantom Kit" from the drop down menu.
5. The current coil field will be automatically filled in, based on the CoilID of the coil connected to the LPCA. Enter the serial number of the coil being tested in the Coil Serial number field.
6. Click on [Start] to begin the automated test. Depending on the number of test locations (complexity of the coil) the test may take from 3 to 20 minutes.
7. A pop-up displays asking if you want to continue. Click on [Yes].
8. Upon start-up, a Note stating, "Phantom placement and coil landmarking are critical for repeatable results" will appear. If the landmark has been set correctly and there are no air bubbles in the phantom, click [Yes] to continue.
9. When the test is complete, test results display on the screen. The PASS/FAIL status shows PASS if all coil elements are functioning properly. If any coil elements display "FAIL", call the GE Service Representative for coil repair.
10. Click on [Quit] button to exit MCQA Tool.
anchor: From Common Service Desktop (CSD) go to Service Browser and select [Image Quality], "Multi-Coil QA Tool" and then "Click here to start this tool"

product_system: 3.0T Head, Neck, Spine Coil (P/N 5367722)
title: Troubleshooting 3T HNS Coil No Signal or Partial Signal
body: Problem: Unable to pre-scan or receiving no signal, or receiving partial signal from coil elements. Steps: 1. Verify that the port(s) that the coil is plugged into has a green light illuminated (Port A or Port B) or a green lock (Port P1, P2, P3 or P4) indicated. This indicates the coil is properly plugged into the system and the coil I.D. on the coil is properly installed. 2. Verify that the system has correctly detected the coil by checking in the "Currently Connected" in the GUI to select coils in Rx. 3. Verify that the landmark is correct and that the cradle (patient bed) has not unlatched. 4. Verify that the scan locations and any FOV offsets are correct. 5. Visually inspect all coaxial connectors and pins on the system plug. If there are any broken, deformed or recessed pins or coaxial connectors, replace the damaged cable. 6. Verify that the coil is positioned with the cable exiting towards the bore. 7. If you still cannot get a signal, try to scan (transmit and receive) with the body coil. Be sure to remove the imaging coil from the magnet bore before you scan with the body coil. If you still receive no signal the problem probably lies with the MR system. If the scan completes successfully, there is probably a problem with the HNS coil. Contact GE for further assistance. 8. You may also try to scan with a similar type (receive only) coil. If you are unable to scan with this coil, there may be a system problem related to this particular coil type.
anchor: Verify that the port(s) that the coil is plugged into has a green light illuminated (Port A or Port B) or a green lock (Port P1, P2, P3 or P4) indicated.

product_system: 3.0T Head, Neck, Spine Coil (P/N 5367722)
title: Troubleshooting Poor Image Quality or MCQA Failure
body: 1. Visually inspect all coaxial connectors and pins on the system plug. If there are any broken, deformed or recessed pins or coaxial connectors, replace the damaged cable. 2. Verify that there are no loops in the cables. 3. Verify that there are no metal or ferromagnetic objects close to the coil, patient or magnet (i.e., safety pin, hair pin). 4. Verify that the coil is properly positioned. 5. Verify that your center frequency is within the frequency adjustment range for your system. 6. Verify that the R1, R2 and TG values from the pre-scan are within normally expected ranges. 7. Perform a system Quality Assurance MCQA test. 8. If values do not fall within normal operating parameters, perform a phantom scan with the body coil (remove imaging coil from magnet bore before scan). 9. If body coil scan is satisfactory, acquire a scan using another coil of the same type and same system coil selection. 10. If image quality is visibly improved with another coil, there may be a problem with the Head Neck Spine coil - contact GE for further assistance.
anchor: Visually inspect all coaxial connectors and pins on the system plug. If there are any broken, deformed or recessed pins or coaxial connectors, replace the damaged cable.

title: Troubleshooting Black Line, Strip Lines, or Signal Void Artifacts
body: 1. Verify that there is no metal present in the area being scanned in, or on the patient. 2. Verify that no hair is trapped in the connectors between the anterior and posterior sections of the head unit. This may appear as intermittent oscillations. 3. Verify the cable connector of the NCU is fully engaged into the receptacle on the posterior section of the head unit. If the connector is not fully engaged, there may be a coil not present error or there may be intermittent oscillations. 4. If you have oscillation of the preamp you will see striped lines.

product_system: 16Ch Diagnostic Breast Coil P-H16LE-030-01893, GE 3.0T (GEHC P/N 5772248)
title: MCQA Test Procedure for 16Ch Diagnostic Breast Coil
body: 1. From Common Service Desktop (CSD), go to Service Browser and select [Image Quality] 'Multi-Coil QA Tool' and then 'Click here to start this tool'. 2. If a 'No valid MCR-V (or MCR2/3)' warning pops up click [Yes] and proceed with test. 3. Choose entry ending as 'Left_Array' or 'Right_Array' for the test with the phantom placed inside the left or the right cavity of the coil. Enter the serial number of the coil being tested in the field 'Coil Serial #'. 4. Click [Start] to begin the automated test. The test may take from 3-5 minutes depending on the MR system. 5. Upon start-up, a message stating 'Phantom placement and coil landmarking are critical for repeatable results' will appear. If the landmark has been set correctly and there are no air bubbles in the phantom, click [Yes] to continue. 6. After the test has been completed, test results are displayed on the screen. The PASS/FAIL status shows PASS if all coil elements are functioning properly. 7. Perform the test for the other cavity of the coil. The test for both cavities must result in PASS. 8. Click on [Quit] button to exit MCQA Tool.
anchor: Click [Start] to begin the automated test as shown in Figure 4. The test may take from 3-5 minutes depending on the MR system.

doc_title: GEM Flex Coil, 1.5T and 3.0T Service Manual (NeoCoil NC021SCM)
product_system: GEM Flex Coil, 1.5T and 3.0T
title: Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) Coil and Phantom Setup
body: 1. Remove any other surface coils or pads from the table. 2. Place the appropriate phantom on the table in the R/L and S/I directions. When using two brick phantoms, ensure that the phantoms are aligned with and touching each other. 3. Lay the 16-L array lengthwise on top of the phantoms, with the spine of the array (cable exit) on top of the intersection of the phantoms. Ensure cable exits to the right of the bore. If testing a 3.0T 16-L array, secure the array to the phantom using a strap. Position the 16-S and 16-M arrays so that the spine of the array (cable exit) is resting on the table. 4. Plug the connector from the antenna into the interface, ensuring that the connection is secure. A green LED light on the interface will illuminate when the array is connected. 5. Route the system cable down the center of the table, taking care to avoid looping the cable. 6. Landmark on the center of the array. 7. From the MR service desktop window, Image quality tab, select Multi-Coil QA Tool. 8. Confirm that the serial number in the MCQA tool matches the equipment being tested.
anchor: Route the system cable down the center of the table, taking care to avoid looping the cable.

product_system: GEM Flex Coil, 1.5T and 3.0T
title: QA for GEM Flex Pediatric Interface
body: 1. Remove any other surface coils or pads from the table. 2. Place the NeoCoil Pediatric Stabilizer on the table oriented in a head-first position. 3. Place your hand in the gap, with your fingers under the cover, and gently pry cover loose. 4. Look through the window in the base of the Stabilizer and make note of the serial number that is applied to the Pediatric Interface. 5. Replace the cover back on to the base of the Stabilizer. 6. Lay the 16-M array on the flat section of the Stabilizer. 7. Plug the connector from the antenna into the interface, ensuring that the connection is secure. A green LED light on the interface will illuminate when the array is connected. 8. Route the system cable down the center of the table, taking care to avoid looping the cable, and plug into the connector at the foot end of the table. 9. Advance the table to the bore and landmark on the center of the array. 10. Place the appropriate phantom on top of the 16-M array so that it is centered on the array. 11. From the MR service desktop window, Image quality tab, select Multi-Coil QA Tool. 12. Enter the serial number for the GEM Flex Pediatric Interface in the MCQA tool. 13. Check for PASS/FAIL in the last column in the Status section.
section: QA for the GEM Flex Pediatric Interface

title: Cable Replacement Procedure
body:
1. Remove the anti-tamper labels.
2. Remove the screws on the cover of the interface, by puncturing the white dot over the screwhead.
3. Loosen the two screws on the bottom of the receptacle bracket shown in Figure 7.
4. Remove screws from old cable and system cable connector (SCC) boards.
5. Attach new cable by carefully routing the wires between the modules and screwing the SCC boards (outlined in Figure 8) in place.
6. Re-attach the cable clamp of the system cable.
7. Replace the cover.
8. Tighten the screws that secure the receptacle bracket, otherwise connection problems are likely to occur.
9. Apply new anti-tamper labels.
10. Run MCQA procedure as described in Installation section.
IMPORTANT: If a pin on any of the SCC boards is bent, return the cable for replacement.
NOTE: Do not write on or mark up the cable being returned.
anchor: If cable fails the continuity check (refer to page 35 in the Troubleshooting section) or if bent or damaged pins are identified then the system cable should be replaced.

doc_title: GEM Flex Coil, 1.5T and 3.0T Service Manual (NeoCoil NC021SCM)
product_system: GEM Flex Coil, 1.5T and 3.0T
title: Replacing foam pocket on array
body: 1. Remove and discard the screw cover decal from the bottom of the spine. 2. Remove and discard the two screw cover plates from the top of the spine. On the 3.0T 16-L array, remove the velcro patch and underlying label from the top of the spine. 3. Remove the screws from the spine - four on top and four on bottom for the 16-S, 16-M, and 1.5T 16-L arrays; and six on top and seven on the bottom for the 3.0T 16-L array - puncturing the white dots on top of the screwheads. 4. Remove spine cover from top of array. 5. Remove the two screws in the cable clamp and take off cover. 6. Remove the middle spine piece, being careful of the wires. On the 3.0T 16-L array, remove the screw below the cable clamp prior to removed the middle spine piece. 7. On the 16-L array only, remove cable ties from the foam pocket leaving the ties wrapped around the wires. 8. Remove the two exposed feed boards on the 16-S and 16-M arrays, or the one feed board on the 1.5T 16-L coil, by unscrewing the feed board(s) and carefully lifting the feed board(s) from the antenna array. The feed board on the 3.0T 16-L does not require removal. 9. Unscrew the screw(s)/washer(s) holding the lower spine piece to the antenna array. 10. Remove the lower spine piece. 11. Remove foam pocket by gently inserting your hand into the pocket, slowly lifting the covers away from the array. 12. Holding down the array with one hand inside the pocket, use your other hand to gently remove the pocket off of the array. 13. Replace left and right foam pockets. NOTE: On the 16-S and 16-M arrays, the end of the array that shows the S/N goes into the pocket with the white flap. With the 16-L array, insert the longer end of the array into the longer foam pocket.
anchor: Remove the screws from the spine - four on top and four on bottom for the 16-S, 16-M, and 1.5T 16-L arrays; and six on top and seven on the bottom for the 3.0T 16-L array

title: Failed MCQA Troubleshooting
body: 1) When MCQA reports failure, run MCQA again with a different antenna but with the same interface. 2) If problem is resolved using a new antenna array, return the bad antenna array and order a new one. 3) If problem remains, check the continuity of the interface cable with a multimeter using the applicable table and diagram. If cable is causing the fault order a new one. You may need to disconnect each SCS board to access the soldered end of each wire. Follow steps for "Cable Replacement" on page 25 to remove the cable for testing and replacing. 4) If problem still persists after ruling out antenna and cable, return the interface for replacement.

title: Bias Fault Message – Troubleshooting
body: If the message log contains a bias fault message: 1. Visually inspect the system cable and antenna for a bent pin. 2. If there is a bent pin in the system cable, return it for a new one. If the bent pin is on the antenna cable, return the antenna. 3. If there is no visibly bent pin, re-run the scan with a different GEM Flex Coil. 4. If the bias fault is not seen with the second coil, return the coil that produced the error. 5. If the bias fault happens again with the second GEM Flex Coil, return the system cable. Do not write on or mark up the cable being returned.
anchor: If the message log contains a bias fault message, visually inspect the system cable and antenna for a bent pin.

title: Pre-work safety requirements for MR service
body:
Before working in any GE Healthcare MR suite or performing any GE Healthcare service procedure, you must:
1. Have read and understood all hazard conditions and safety requirements in the latest revision of the GE Healthcare MR Service Safety Manual (5452735).
2. Have successfully completed all relevant GE Healthcare Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) courses (or for non-GE employees, equivalent workplace training courses).
3. Comply with all site-specific training and workplace safety requirements.
If you have any safety concerns at any time, do not begin work or immediately stop work and move to a safe location. Immediately contact your supervisor or site safety officer for instructions on how to proceed.
anchor: Before working in any GE Healthcare MR suite or performing any GE Healthcare service procedure, you must: • Have read and understood all hazard conditions and safety requirements in the latest revision of the GE Health- care MR Service Safety Manual (5452735).

product_system: SIGNA Prime MAX / SIGNA Prime Elite
title: Examine packages for damage in transportation
body:
Examine all packages closely at delivery. If damage is apparent:
1. Make sure the notation damage in shipment is written on all copies of the freight or express bill before delivery is accepted or signed for by a GE HealthCare representative or a hospital receiving agent.
2. Whether noted or concealed, you must report damage to the carrier immediately upon discovery, or in any event, within 14 days after receipt, and hold the contents and containers for inspection by the carrier. A transportation company will not pay a claim for damage if an inspection is not requested within this 14-day period.

body: Air ride trailers must be used. The magnet must be centered on the trailer with the magnet bore perpendicular to the truck. The magnet must not be positioned over the trailer axles. Crate and/or frame top and sides must not be used to secure the magnet to the trailer. Magnets should be secured to the trailer using crate/magnet base.

product_system: SIGNA Prime MAX / SIGNA Prime Elite
title: Predelivery site visit and planning requirements
body: Before magnet delivery, the GE PMI and rigger must do the following: 1. Visit the magnet site with the rigging foreman before magnet delivery to plan the move. GE PMI must hand-deliver a copy of this document to the rigging foreman. 2. Review the guidelines for shipping/handling and for equipment/tools with the rigging foreman per Unloading and moving the magnet in this manual. 3. Caution the rigger that the magnet is extremely fragile. Sudden jolts can damage the magnet. 4. Make sure all routes and paths leading to the magnet room are level and free from obstacles and holes. 5. Make sure that clearance dimensions along the path to the magnet room meet the requirements stated in the Preinstallation Manual (5941479-8EN). 6. If roller dollies are to be used, have the rigger bring steel plates to put along the delivery route.
anchor: Visit the magnet site with the rigging foreman before magnet delivery to plan the move. GE PMI must hand-deliver a copy of this document to the rigging foreman.

doc_title: SIGNA Prime MAX / SIGNA Prime Elite Magnet Handling Manual
product_system: SIGNA Prime MAX / SIGNA Prime Elite
title: WARNING: Potential injury from unbalanced magnet load and tilting
body:
Magnet is an unbalanced load. Tilting can result in a hazardous condition that can cause magnet damage or serious personal injury. To avoid tilting:
• Make sure that the lifting apparatus (crane, spreader beam, and so on) meets the specifications stated in this manual.
• Adjust the lifting cables/slings and spreader beam (if used) lift point to level the magnet before fully lifting the magnet off the surface.
• Make sure that the entire area where lifting will occur is free of obstructions and unauthorized personnel.
• Make sure the surface where the magnet will be put after lifting is flat.
• Do not crane lift a magnet during dangerous weather conditions.
anchor: Magnet is an unbalanced load. Tilting can result in a hazardous condition that can cause magnet damage or serious personal injury.

body: Improper transportation can result in damage to the magnet. Tasks in this section are to be done by riggers, not by GE HealthCare Personnel. Weights referenced in section 2.2 Equipment requirements on page 15 are rigging weights (rounded up from actual weights) and are not actual shipping weights. Refer to magnet shipping documents for actual weights of the magnet and crate. Do not use a crane to lift a magnet that is on a pallet or inside a crate. Crane lifting can only be done using the magnet lifting holes, which are not accessible while the magnet is inside the crate.

title: Removing subsystem crates
body:
1. Carefully inspect all packaging for damage that may have occurred during shipping.
2. Remove all subsystem crates, except the magnet crate, from the trailer/transport using a crane or forklift. To handle the magnet crate in transit from the truck or plane, see 2.5 Handling the crated magnet in transit with a forklift on page 18.
3. Inspect all crates for visible damage. Report any damage you find in conformance with the 1.2 Examining packages for damage in transportation on page 6 procedure.
4. Move subsystem crates to a receiving location protected from the weather, preferably close to and at the same level as the MR suite/magnet room.

title: Handling the crated magnet in transit with a forklift
body:
1. Put a forklift in position beside the magnet crate/pallet meeting the requirements stated in section 2.2 Equipment requirements on page 15.
2. Carefully insert the forklift forks completely into the holes in the long side of the shipping pallet.
3. Smoothly lift the crate/pallet with the forklift, and move the crate/pallet to the desired location. NOTE: Magnet lift must be perpendicular to magnet bore. Crate slots for forklift are designed to ensure proper lift orientation.
4. Lower the entire package to rest on a flat, smooth surface. Do not rest the magnet/crate/pallet on any surface that is not flat or strong enough to support the magnet/crate/pallet package.

title: Removing the shipping cage
body: 1. Power off the SVU by pressing the button. 2. Turn off the compressor: 2.1. Turn off the compressor drive switch. 2.2. Turn off the compressor main power switch. 3. Disconnect the cables from the magnet (Magnet B, D, E, and P). A Phillips screw needs to be removed when disconnecting the Magnet P - store the screw properly and DO NOT lose it. 4. Using two wrenches (one to hold the backside adapter connection, and one to loosen), disconnect the coldhead compressor lines in the following order: First - coldhead power cable, Second - coldhead helium supply line, Third - coldhead helium return line. 5. Remove the driver-supplied tarp from the shipping cage. 6. Unstrap the cage if any straps were applied. Then unchain the magnet from the flatbed. 7. To remove the shipping cage: Using a crane - 1. Strap the frame in four locations. 2. Lift the cage straight up and move it away from the magnet. Not using a crane - 1. Unbolt the boards on one end of the cage. 2. Move the cage away from the magnet in the other direction.

title: Removing the shipping crate
body: Prerequisites: Complete MR Service Safety Manual (5452735) training and EHS courses. Procedure: 1. Remove the driver-supplied tarp from the shipping crate. 2. Unchain the crate from the flatbed. 3. Put a crane meeting the specifications in Table 2 above the center of the crate. 4. Attach the slings/cable bridles of a spreader beam to the lifting rings on top of the crate. 5. Remove the lag screws along the lower edges of the crate's left and right side panels that secure those panels to the pallet. Do not remove the lag screws securing the crate's front and back end panels to the pallet until after the crate's side panels are secured in their open position. 6. Remove the lag screws securing the crate side panels to the crate end panels. Do not remove the hinges along each crate side panel's upper edge. 7. Pull open the crate's left and right side panels using the rope handle on each side panel. The crate's left and right side panels are hinged along their upper edges.
anchor: Remove the lag screws along the lower edges of the crate's left and right side panels that secure those panels to the pallet.

doc_title: SIGNA Prime MAX / SIGNA Prime Elite Magnet Handling Manual
product_system: SIGNA Prime MAX / SIGNA Prime Elite
title: Removing the shipping crate
body: 1. Swing the wooden block found inside each vertical corner of the crate outward. 2. Attach the loose end of each block to the adjoining side panel using one of the lag screws removed previously. 3. Remove the lag screws along the lower edges of the crate's front and back end panels that secure those panels to the pallet. 4. Tighten the slings/cable bridles and carefully begin lifting the crate. If the crate does not remain approximately level, carefully lower the crate and adjust the lifting configuration, then lift the crate again. 5. Using the crane, lift the crate top off the magnet's shipping pallet and fully above and clearing the magnet. 6. Put the crate in a clear area. 7. Unbolt and remove the four bolts (one per magnet foot) securing the magnet feet to the pallet. 8. Visually examine the witness marks on each bolt and lifting bracket at each of the four magnet feet. Look for witness mark misalignment between the nut/bolt head and the lifting bracket. 9. If witness marks are aligned correctly, continue. If witness marks do not align: Make sure the brackets are installed against the magnet feet at all four locations. Look inside of the magnet foot. If a through bolt is used (new process), make sure the lock washer is compressed under the bolt head. If it is not, tighten the bolt until the lock washer is compressed. Use a permanent marker to add a new witness mark only on the bolt or nut that was just torqued. 10. Rig and lift the magnet off the pallet in conformance with section 2.8 or section 2.9.
anchor: Unbolt and remove the four bolts (one per magnet foot) securing the magnet feet to the pallet.

title: Checking witness marks on magnet feet bolts
body: If witness marks do not align: 1. Make sure the brackets are installed against the magnet feet at all four locations. 2. Look inside of the magnet foot. If a through bolt is used (new process), make sure the lock washer is compressed under the bolt head. If it is not, tighten the bolt until the lock washer is compressed. 3. Use a permanent marker to add a new witness mark only on the bolt or nut that was just torqued.

body: Before moving the magnet through a raised opening in an exterior wall: 1) Complete a walk-through of the crane lift process prior to actual event to ensure all process details are covered. 2) Ensure all necessary equipment is on-site and inspected for safety and load ratings. 3) Ensure all necessary personnel are trained and ready. 4) Ensure entire area where lifting will occur is free of obstructions and unauthorized personnel. 5) Ensure surface where magnet will be placed after lifting is flat. 6) Do not crane lift a magnet during dangerous weather conditions.

title: Equipment damage warnings for crane lifting magnet
body: To avoid expensive internal damage: 1) Avoid sudden jolts - lift/move/lower the magnet smoothly. 2) Do not allow magnet to bump or hit anything forcefully. 3) Avoid tilting magnet more than maximum tilt (30° from horizontal level). 4) Do not apply any force to magnet enclosures. 5) Do not crane lift a magnet that is on a pallet or inside a cage or crate. 6) Crane lifting can only be done using magnet lifting rails, not accessible while magnet is inside cage or crate.

title: Converting an air magnet shipment to warehouse configuration
body: Prerequisites: 2 persons, 15 minutes preliminary, 30 minutes procedure. Steps: 1. Confirm the magnet pressure gauge shows positive pressure. Resolve any negative readings before moving on. 2. Cut off the zip-tie securing the relief valve. 3. Open the relief valve and vent the magnet pressure until there is no visible helium gas coming out of the port. Then, shut the valve. Make sure the magnet pressure remains positive for the entire time. 4. Locate and remove the blind plate under the pressure gauge. Be careful to not drop the O-ring positioning ring and the O-ring. 5. Install the pressure transducer and tighten the clamp.

title: Preparing scan room for leveling magnet
body:
1. Make sure markings are present on magnet room floor (isocenter location and z-axis vector, or isocenter and vent pipe center).
2. If needed, transcribe marks from ceiling to floor with tape from kit, using laser levels.
3. Align positioning template (5926243-301-31) to markings (center-line with z-axis vector, or to isocenter and vent stack location).
4. Use tape from kit to secure positioning template to floor.
5. Make sure first laser level is in self-leveling mode.
6. Position first laser level on tripod in front of room.
7. Adjust laser line to pass through isocenter along z-axis vector.
8. Mark at least two reference locations (one close, one far away) on floor/wall/ceiling; do not mark where magnet will be set; ensure marks visible when magnet in position.
9. Make sure second laser level is in self-leveling mode.
10. Position second laser level on tripod on left side (electronics side).
11. Adjust second laser until vertical line passes through lateral (x-dir) centerline axis on template and visible on magnet cryogen chamber when in position.
12. Mark at least two reference locations (one close, one far away) on floor/wall/ceiling; do not mark where magnet will be set; ensure marks visible when magnet in position.
13. Remove template from floor.
14. Continue to appropriate chapter (non-seismic: Chapter 6; seismic: Chapter 7).

title: Lowering the magnet into position
body:
1. Cut and remove enough of the bubble wrap to allow access to the feet for leveling operations. NOTE: When cutting off the bubble wrap, do not nick or cut any electrical cables.
2. Align the holes in the magnet feet to the anchor holes in the vibroacoustic damping mats.
3. Make sure that the four holes, one per each magnet foot, align centered ±3mm (±0.125inches) over the anchor stud holes in the vibroacoustic damping mats.
4. Jack the magnet up sufficiently at the four angle brackets (four corners) and remove the moving fixtures.
5. Put the damping mats below the magnet feet, ensure that the magnet feet can be fully covered.
6. Slowly lower the magnet onto the damping mats.

title: Leveling the magnet (nonseismic vibroacoustic damping mat)
body: 1. Make sure the laser level is in self-leveling mode. (In self-leveling mode, if the laser level tilts > 4° in any direction, the lasers do not show. When the laser level tilt is ≤ 4°, the level indicator LED is green and the lasers show.) 2. Set up laser on the front of magnet and adjust height to 1070mm (42.13 inches). Set 1070mm (42.13 inches) as the leveling target. (If necessary, position a folding ruler vertically near the front center of the magnet, and adjust the tripod height until the horizontal laser line aligns on the ruler 1070 mm (42.13 inches) from the floor (the magnet isocenter should be 1070 ± 6 mm).) 3. Check the four marks (3 and 9 o'clock) of the front and rear on the gradient coil with horizontal laser line. 3.1. If the highest mark is above 1070mm (42.13 inches), and it is in the range of 1070mm (42.13 inches) ~1076mm (42.36 inches), take the measurement of the highest height as the leveling target. 3.2. If all marks below the laser line, remain 1070mm (42.13 inches) as the leveling target. 4. Leveling the magnet by inserting shim pads (there are 1mm shims and 3mm shims) between damping mats under the magnet feet. Make all four marks on magnet overlapped with the laser line. (Make sure that the U-shaped holes align centered ±3mm over the anchor stud holes in the vibroacoustic damping mats and the shim pads fully cover the magnet feet.) 5. Recheck markers on the magnet, make sure all the markers not exceed 1076mm (42.36 inches) or under 1064mm (41.89 inches). 6. Test-fit the cryogen vent stack to make sure it aligns with the scan room vent pipe. 7. Remove the lifting angle brackets (5926243-302-23).
anchor: Set up laser on the front of magnet and adjust height to 1070mm (42.13 inches). Set 1070mm (42.13 inches) as the leveling target.

2. Move the magnet to align the holes in the magnet feet to the anchor holes in the vibroacoustic damping mats.
3. Make sure that the four holes, one per each magnet foot, align centered ± 3 mm (± 0.125 inches) over the seismic anchor holes in the vibroacoustic mats.
4. Jack the magnet up sufficiently at the four lifting angle brackets, and remove the moving fixtures.
5. Slowly lower the magnet onto the vibroacoustic mats. Make sure the threaded seismic rods go through the holes in the magnet feet.
anchor: Slowly lower the magnet onto the vibroacoustic mats. Make sure the threaded seismic rods go through the holes in the magnet feet.

title: Leveling the magnet
body: 1. Make sure the laser level is in self-leveling mode. (In self-leveling mode, if the laser level tilts > 4° in any direction, the lasers do not show. When the laser level tilt is ≤ 4°, the level indicator LED is green and the lasers show.) 2. Set up laser on the front of magnet and adjust height to 1070mm (42.13 inches). Set 1070mm (42.13 inches) as the leveling target. (If necessary, position a folding ruler vertically near the front center of the magnet, and adjust the tripod height until the horizontal laser line aligns on the ruler 1070 mm (42.13 inches) from the floor.) 3. Check the four marks (3 and 9 o'clock) of the front and rear on the gradient coil with horizontal laser line. 3.1. If the highest mark is above 1070mm (42.13 inches), and it is in the range of 1070mm (42.13 inches) ~1076mm (42.36 inches), take the measurement of the highest height as the leveling target. 3.2. If all marks below the laser line, remain 1070mm (42.13 inches) as the leveling target. 4. Leveling the magnet by inserting shim pads (there are 1mm shims and 3mm shims) between damping mats under the magnet feet. Make all four marks on magnet overlapped with the laser line. (Make sure that the U-shaped holes align centered ±3mm over the anchor stud holes in the vibroacoustic damping mats and the shim pads fully cover the magnet feet.) 5. Recheck markers on the magnet, make sure all the markers not exceed 1076mm (42.36 inches) or under 1064mm (41.89 inches). 6. Test-fit the cryogen vent stack to make sure it aligns with the scan room vent pipe. 7. Remove the lifting angle brackets (5926243-302-23).
anchor: Set up laser on the front of magnet and adjust height to 1070mm (42.13 inches). Set 1070mm (42.13 inches) as the leveling target.

title: Seismic mounting of vibroacoustic damping mat to floor
body: 1. Install the rubber collar (5822743) from the seismic anchor kit (M6001AH) on the inner diameter of the magnet foot. 2. Put the stainless steel center ring (5817180) from the kit on the threaded seismic rod. 3. Screw three of the M14 screws (1000-M14C050-31) from the kit into the stainless steel mounting plate (5817179) until the screws reaches the inner diameter of the plate. 4. Put the mounting plate through the opening in the magnet foot, around the seismic rod and over the center ring, with the flush side of the plate pointed toward the ceiling. Make sure the flat edge of the mounting plate points toward the opening in the magnet foot. 5. Screw four of the M10 screws (1000-M10C035-31) from the kit through the mounting bracket and engage the threads into the magnet foot. Using a ratchet or wrench, firmly tighten the M10 screws. 6. Hand-tighten the three M14 screws up to the center ring. If needed, use the hex tool (5822744) from the kit to help in tightening. 7. Put an appropriately sized flange nut on the seismic stud. Hand-tighten the flange nut toward the mounting plate; then back off one full turn to make sure there is a gap between the flange nut and the mounting plate. 8. Put a Nord-Lock washer on top of the flange nut. 9. Put a jam nut on top of the Nord-Lock washer and hand-tighten. 10. Using two wrenches, tighten the jam nut while keeping the flange nut in position. Make sure there is still a gap between the flange nut and the mounting plate.

title: Installing the rear endbell
body:
Personnel: 1 person, Procedure time: 30 minutes.
1. Align rear endbell with rear of magnet, partially insert the rear endbell.

product_system: TEAL PDU Module in XGD2 Cabinet
title: Input Voltage Selection Configuration
body:
To configure PDU for nominal input voltages (380, 400, 415, or 480 VAC three phase):
1. On the Main Disconnect Panel (MDP), turn off the PDU circuit breaker, lock and tag appropriately.
2. Using a voltmeter or other voltage indicating device at the Main Input Terminal Board, check to be sure that no voltage is being applied to the input of the PDU.
3. Remove the small cover panels from the front panel of the PDU marked "INPUT VOLTAGE SELECT".
4. For each of the three phases, be sure the wire is connected to the proper terminal for the actual input voltage at the site and that the terminal screw is tight to make a good connection. (TB1 shown configured for 480V Delta in Illustration 3-1)
anchor: The PDU allows for nominal input voltages of 380, 400, 415, or 480 VAC (three phase).

product_system: TEAL PDU Module in XGD2 Cabinet
title: Maintenance and FRU Replacement General Procedure
body:
No maintenance is required other than periodically (i.e. every 6 months) all electrical connections should be checked for tightness. Accumulations of dust or debris should be removed from front panel to keep ventilation working for convection cooling.

To replace FRU components:
1. First shutoff and lockout power.
2. Remove necessary panels.
3. Locate proper component (refer to Location drawing).
4. Replace with new component (refer to FRU table).
5. Reinstall all panels and restore power.
anchor: To replace FRU components – First shutoff and lockout power, remove necessary panels, locate proper component (refer to Location drawing below) and replace with new component (refer to FRU table below).

product_system: TEAL PDU Module in XGD2 Cabinet
title: Removal of Front Panel to Access Additional FRUs
body: Tools needed: Phillips screwdriver or power screwdriver set, 11/32 open wrench. 1. Turn off the main input circuit breaker by rotating the lever to the off position. Perform the lockout-tagout (LOTO) procedure at the MDP. 2. Remove the 4 (6-32 x 3/8) screws on the circuit breaker guard using a Phillips screwdriver. 3. Remove the 12 (10-32x1/2) screws on the front panel using Phillips screwdriver. 4. Slightly pull the front panel and lean it down and away from the unit. Be careful not to damage the leak sensor strip. 5. Disconnect SW1 and SW2 from the back of the front panel. No tools are required. Turn tabs counterclockwise and gently pull assembly apart.

doc_title: TEAL PDU Module in XGD2 Cabinet (GE Part Number 5343114)
product_system: TEAL PDU Module in XGD2 Cabinet
title: Replacement of the Control PC Board
body: 1. Remove the front panel as per 4.1.2. 2. Remove the four mounting screws (8-32 x 3") from the circuit breaker (CB2) and move the CB to the side. Do not discard screws. 3. Using the tool supplied with the PCB, pop the PCBA off the front two nylon posts. The lower post can be accessed through the port hole. 4. With an ESD strap on, gently slide the PCBA out of the rear holders. Ensure that the toggle position of SW1 is properly set and has not been altered during the removal of the board. 5. Disconnect cables P1, P2, P3, A1-P5, A1-P6, A1-P7, A1-P8. Mark the cables with masking tape and marker to ensure correct position when re-connecting. 6. Configure the replacement of the PDU Control board according to the cabinet type. All boards should be shipped with the board set to the AUX position. Replace the board according to the instructions in 4.1.7 (the above instructions in reverse order). 7. When reinstalling the board ensure that P6 connector bundle is seated behind porthole and beneath the PC Control board toggle switch.

anchor: Remove the four mounting screws from the circuit breaker (CB2) and move the CB to the side.

product_system: TEAL PDU Module in XGD2 Cabinet
title: Verify Proper PDU Control Board Replacement
body: 1. TURN OFF ALL CIRCUIT BREAKERS ON THE PDU BEFORE CONTINUING TO AVOID UNNECCESSARY POWER CYCLING TO OTHER SYSTEM COMPONENTS. 2. Once the front cover is re-installed, apply power to PDU and PGR cabinet by turning on the main input circuit breaker (CB1) and then the Gradient 48V Control circuit breaker (CB9) to power up the PEM/AUX Module. Inspect the control board through the upper right vent holes in the front cover and verify the appropriate configuration LED is on (located above the configuration switch): Green indicates XGD configuration; Yellow indicates XGD II configuration. 3. After configuration confirmation, perform the leak sensor functionality check in accordance with the "System Power On" service direction under the installation -> system folder located within the product's service methods. Re-check PDU Control board set-up and cabling if this fails. 4. Verify the functionality of the E-stop circuitry in accordance with the "Emergency Stop and Off Check" service direction under the Functional Checks -> System folder located within the product's service methods. Once these tests are completed, you may apply power to the rest of the components in the system.

title: Incorrect PDU Control Board Configuration Warning
body: Incorrect replacement or configuration of the PDU Control Board may immediately activate Emergency Off and cause main PDU CB1 to trip and open. This will happen if the PDU Control Board with PEM configuration is installed inside an XGD PGR cabinet which contains an XGD Auxiliary "AUX" Module. When the main PDU CB1 is closed, incoming power is applied the PDU Control Board. Once this board boots, it will immediately activate Emergency Off and cause main PDU CB1 to trip and open.
