title: Replacement of Fans (FAN1 or FAN2) for units PN 6550012-06 Rev A3 and Prior
body: Tools needed: Phillips screwdriver or power screwdriver set, 5/16 open end wrench (small). CAUTION - Care must be taken so that hardware does not fall down into the unit. Step 1: Remove the front panel as per 4.1.2. Step 2: Remove 3 (10-32x1/2) screws at the Anderson assembly connector. Note: Do not discard screws, they will be used to replace assembly. Step 3: Remove fans (FAN1 and FAN2) by unscrewing 4 (6-32 x 2) screws using Phillips screwdriver. Note: Do not discard screws; they will be used to replace fan assembly. Step 4: Unplug fan connectors. Step 5: If left fan (FAN1) needs replacing, right fan (FAN2) must be removed first to allow wrench access. Using wrench, loosen nuts, just enough to break the lock, on the fan. Step 6: Use Philips head screw drive to back out the screws, just to the point that the fan separates from the back panel. Step 7: Once the fan on the right is completely removed you can now access the nuts on the left fan, following the instructions above. Step 8: When the old fans are out and away from the unit, remove the screws completely retaining ONE of the locking nuts and the fan guard.

title: Replacement of CB1 Shunt Trip
body: If the circuit breaker shunt trip is deemed defective as per the Troubleshooting Guide in 4.1.16 follow the steps below. 1. On the front of CB1, remove the 4 screws holding the circuit breaker handle in place. 2. Remove the handle from the circuit breaker. 3. Remove the remaining 3 screws to remove the circuit breaker cover. 4. Remove the shunt trip from the left side of the circuit breaker by pulling straight up on the pull tab. Cut the shunt trip wires to fully remove the old shunt trip. 5. Insert the JG adapter on the shunt trip. 6. Insert the new shunt trip into the circuit breaker and route the wires. Butt splice the new shunt trip's wires with the old wires. 7. Reattach the circuit breaker cover using ONLY the 3 screws removed in step 3. 8. Place the handle removed in step 2 over the circuit breaker and secure using the remaining 4 screws removed in step 1.

body: NOTE: It is recommended to only replace the TB slots used for the transformer taps to minimize risk of miswiring. 1. Identify the transformer tap configuration and note their positions along the terminal block. 2. Disconnect wires 4-6 from the top of TB1 using a flathead screwdriver. title: Replacement of Power Supplies (PS1 & PS2)
body: 1. For both XGD and XGD2, remove the 3 (10-32x1/2) screws at the receptacle assembly. Move the assembly out of the way. Do not recycle the screws. Use Masking Tape and Marker to mark these wires. 2. If more space is necessary, mark wires attached to the circuit breaker(s), then disconnect the wires. 3. Alternatively, remove the mounting screws from the circuit breaker(s) and move the circuit breaker to the side. Do not recycle screws. 4. Remove the 2 Kep nuts and 2 washers at the power supply assembly. Remove the 2 Kep nuts and 2 washers at the ground wires (if necessary, use a cutter to the tie wrap to allow slack for the power supply harness). Do not recycle the nuts and washers. 5. Carefully pull out the power supply assembly by lifting the assembly over the studs and sliding forward out of the front from the unit. Make sure to move the RF cable out of the way. 6. Mark the wire Run numbers/description on the wires with masking tape and a marker. Disconnect ALL wires from the Condor power supply assembly. Proper marking of the wire numbers is critical. 7. Attach the marked Condor wires to the terminal strip on the Delta bracket – note the Delta labeling shows the run number and the terminal block number with description (pin # 1 is on the left).
anchor: If the power supplies are deemed defective, follow the steps below to replace the power supplies.

title: Assemble Delta Power Supply with Existing Bracket
body:

2. Slide first power supply PS2 (FRU 5745311) into bottom slot of bracket.

6. Attach PS1 connector to rear of PS1. Note: PS1 harness only reaches PS1 supply.

doc_title: TEAL PDU Module in XGD2 Cabinet (GE Part Number 5343114)
product_system: TEAL PDU Module in XGD2 Cabinet
title: Move CON1 auxiliary contact wires from NC to NO when replacing Condor with Delta
body:
For XGD:
1. The auxiliary contact terminals can be accessed from the front. If you need more room to work, gently push in the light gray tab on the base of the AUX SW to release auxiliary switch from CON1.
2. Use a Philips screwdriver to disconnect wire 97 from the N/C contact, terminal 21 and remove the wire to the N/O contact, terminal 13. Do the same for wire 98, moving it from the N/C contact, terminal 22 to the N/O contact, terminal 14.
3. Push the light gray tab to reinsert AUX SW onto CON1.

For XGD2:
4. Insert a small flat-head screwdriver between contactor CON1 and the auxiliary contact. Gently pry the auxiliary contact away from the contactor.
5. Use a Philips screwdriver to disconnect wire 97 from the N/C contact, terminal 21 and remove the wire to the N/O contact, terminal 13. Do the same for wire 98, moving it from the N/C contact, terminal 22 to the N/O contact, terminal 14.
6. Once the wires have been moved, push the auxiliary contact to the contactor, CON1 when the peg and clips of the auxiliary contact are aligned. An audible "click" will be heard when the auxiliary contact is fully inserted back onto the contactor.
7. Reinstall the front panel. Be careful not to damage the leak sensor strip.
8. Apply maintenance sticker (5661793) noting that the Delta supplies are installed on the front of the PDU.
anchor: the auxiliary contact wires (97 and 98) on CON1 contactor must be moved from the (NC) Normally Closed to (NO) Normally Open location.

title: ML15.121 Battery Charging Configuration
body: To use power supply for float-charging 12V lead-acid or VRLA batteries: 1) Ensure ambient temperature does not exceed 50°C. 2) Set output voltage precisely to end-of-charge voltage per battery temperature: 10°C=13.9V, 20°C=13.75V, 30°C=13.6V, 40°C=13.4V. 3) Use a 2A or 3A circuit breaker (or blocking diode) between power supply and battery. 4) Ensure output current is below allowed charging current of battery. 5) Use only matched batteries when putting 6V types in series. Return current is typ. 12mA at 12.5Vdc when power supply switched off.

body: WARNING: This cryocooler (cold head, compressor unit, compressor adsorber, flex lines) contains a high-pressure (about 1.62 MPa) helium gas sealed in. Hitting the equipment with a sharp edge or touching it with a pointed object may cause explosion or escape of gas. Handle the equipment with extreme care. Install the cryocooler in the ventilated area, otherwise it may result in asphyxiation in case the helium gas is purged or leaked.

doc_title: Gradient Test Sequence
product_system: Gradtest pulse sequence (Research and Service mode)
title: Gradient Test Sequence Setup and Execution
body: 1. Remove the gradient amplifier protective cover. 2. Connect the oscilloscope to the current monitor connector located on the gradient amplifier being tested. 3. Go into service mode. 4. On the Scan Setup screen, select Single Scan and List All, and then select GradTest from the list of sequences. 5. Setup the pulse sequence controls: a. Frequency (ramp time) = 500, b. Phase (gradient strength) = 100, c. TE (total pulse duration) = 5000, d. TR = 1000, e. RF Spoiling option checked turns on the X gradient, Partial Data option checked turns on the Y gradient, and No Phase Wrap option checked turns on the Z gradient, f. Select manual prescan. 6. Select Begin Protocol: a. In the Manual Prescan window, click RG mode, b. Observe the waveform on the oscilloscope.

product_system: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus
title: Dropped Probe Testing Procedure
body:
Never use a probe that has fallen to the floor. Even if it looks OK, it may be damaged, possibly resulting in misdiagnosis. Before returning the probe to use, perform the following tests:
1. Perform safety testing per this service manual or per IEC62353.
2. Test that the probe function as intended.
If the probe fails any of the tests, contact your GE HealthCare representative.

title: Charge Box Assembly/Disassembly Procedure
body:
1. Press on/off button on the ultrasound system to turn off the system.
2. Disconnect the power source to the ultrasound system.
3-4. Use one hand to press down the lock lever of the rotary push-to-close latch while at the same time use the other hand to pull out the charge box.
5. Carefully push battery box into main frame with both hands. When the Charge Box is fully installed on the system, the latch will automatically lock.
6. Connect the power source to the ultrasound system.
7. Press on/off button on the ultrasound system to turn on the system.
anchor: (1)Press on/off button on the ultrasound system to turn off the system.

title: Pre-call information to gather before contacting Customer Care
body:
Before calling for support, identify and prepare the following information and acquire image (Alt+D) to send to Customer Care:
1. Ultrasound system ID serial number.
2. Software version.
3. Date and time of occurrence.
4. Sequence of events leading to issue.
5. Is the issue repeatable?
6. Imaging mode, probe, preset/application.
7. Media brand, speed, capacity, type.
8. Save secondary image capture, cine loop, 4D multi-volume loop.
9. Detailed description of any problem encountered.
10. Where applicable, save the appropriate log files.
Remember to save the log files for each day on a separate media, labelled accordingly.
anchor: Before you call, identify the following information and acquire image (Alt+D) to send to the Customer Care team:

title: External Device Connection System Compliance - DANGER
body: External devices not verified by GE HealthCare can be used only if in compliance with related IEC or ISO Safety standards (eg. 60601/62368 series). Conformance to IEC/EN60601-1 Clause 16 requirements for whole system must be verified. Accessory equipment connected to analog and digital interfaces must be certified according to respective IEC or ISO Safety standards (e.g. IEC/EN62368-1 for data processing equipment or IEC/EN60601-1 for medical equipment). All complete configurations shall comply with requirements for Medical Electrical systems of IEC/EN60601-1. Anyone connecting additional equipment to signal input or output part configures a medical electrical system and is responsible that system complies with IEC/EN60601-1 Clause 16.

anchor: Anybody connecting additional equipment to the signal input part or signal output part of the ultrasound system configures a medical electrical system, and is therefore responsible that the system complies with the requirements of the IEC/EN60601-1 Clause 16.

title: Patient environment peripheral connection precautions - on-board devices
body: General precautions for installing an alternate on-board device: 1. The added device must have appropriate safety standard conformance and CE Marking. 2. The total power consumption of the added devices, which connect to the ultrasound system and are used simultaneously, must be less than or equal to the rated supply of the ultrasound system. 3. There must be adequate heat dissipation and ventilation to prevent overheating of the device. 4. There must be adequate mechanical mounting of the device and stability of the combination. 5. Risk and leakage current of the combination must comply with IEC/EN 60601-1. 6. Electromagnetic emissions and immunity of the combination must conform to IEC/EN 60601-1-2.

product_system: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus
title: Connect ultrasound system to power source
body: 1. Ensure that the wall outlet is of appropriate type. 2. Uncoil the power cable, allowing sufficient slack so that the ultrasound system can be moved slightly. 3. Verify that the power cable is without any visible scratches or any sign of damage. 4. Verify that the on-site mains voltage is within the limits indicated on the rating label near the Circuit Breaker at the rear of the ultrasound system. 5. Verify that the Mains Power Circuit Breaker is in OFF position. If not, switch it OFF. 6. If not already done, connect the mains power cable's female plug to the power inlet at the rear of the ultrasound system, then pull down the pull-out protection for power cable. 7. Connect the power cable's other end (male plug) to a hospital grade mains power outlet with the proper rated voltage.
section: 4.1.3.1.2 Connecting the Ultrasound System to a Power Source
anchor: Verify that the on-site mains voltage is within the limits indicated on the rating label near the Circuit Breaker at the rear of the ultrasound system.

Press once on the On/Off key on the Operating Panel to display the System - Exit menu. 3. Select Shutdown to do a complete power down of the ultrasound system. 4. Switch off the Mains Power Circuit Breaker, located at the rear of the ultrasound system. 5. Disconnect the mains power cable.

title: Uncrating Vivid Explorer/Advanced/Focus from cardboard box
body: Before cutting the straps, check the Tilt Tags to make sure they have not been triggered. If damaged, report it to the carrier. If not, continue: 1. Cut the straps around the crate (hold the strap clasp with one hand when cutting). 2. Remove the Top Cover. 3. Remove the three Plastic Locks (press the inside plastic lock gently to release it, then remove the outside lock). 4. Open the sidewall cardboard and remove it. 5. Remove the dust bag from the system. 6. Cut the wrapping bag by scissors and remove the PE bag from the system. 7. Unlock the strap (press the metal part with your thumb, and use your other hand to pull out the packing strap).
anchor: Before cutting the straps, check the Tilt Tags to make sure they have not been triggered.

title: Install Optional Update Kit (4D to Dimension example)
body:
1. Press Utility → Config on the Touch Panel and log on as ADM.
2. Select the Admin category and Licenses subgroup.
3. Press the New button to enter the option key for Vivid Explorer Dimension and then press Save.
4. Ensure that the option key for Vivid Explorer Dimension is listed.
5. Reboot the ultrasound system to ensure the name 'Vivid Explorer Dimension' is correctly displayed on the boot‑up screen.
6. For H48822DE(4D to Dimension Update), apply the Dimension monitor sticker to the lower‑right corner of the monitor. For H48822DD(2D to 4D Update), ignore this step.

title: LED1 ACBOX Power OK - troubleshooting
body: LED1 indicates AC Power BOX 12V DC output power to TMBE is OK. Connect AC power and switch AC breaker to on position. If LED1 light on or PWR_BTN's white LED backlight on OPIO panel light on, mostly ACBOX works fine. If LED1 does not light, consider ACBOX failure. Try to switch AC break to OFF position and unplug power cord for at least 1 minute, then plug back and switch on again. If ACBOX recover and output can work normally, nothing else need. Otherwise, replace ACBOX.
anchor: If LED1 does not light, consider ACBOX failure. Try to switch AC break to OFF position and unplug power cord for at least 1 minute

doc_title: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus General Service Manual
product_system: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus
title: LED4 MST PWR OK - troubleshooting and causes
body: LED4 indicates MSP MCU, DSP, FPGA power up is ok on TMX board. If LED4 does not light on after LED2 is lighted (normally several seconds), mostly TMX board need replacement. On some situations, try install newest software (with VividFirmwareUpdater) first before replacing TMX, some failures may be caused by firmware and software miss match, this can be fixed by software reloading, do not need hardware replace. LED4 shows whether the FPGA and MCU on the TMX have completed the firmware loading and initialization process and have asserted the PWR_OK signal. Possible causes include: Hardware issues, such as a faulty TMX board that may require replacement; Firmware issues, which may be resolved by reloading or reinstalling the software using the VividFirmwareUpdater built into the SW; Software issues, or an unexpected power loss during a firmware upgrade, the firmware can be repaired by reloading or reinstalling the software using the VividFirmwareUpdater built into the SW.
anchor: If LED4 does not light on after LED2 is lighted (normally several seconds), mostly TMX board need replacement.

title: Setup Network Proxy Settings
body: 1. Press the Proxy Settings button on the Connectivity > Network configuration screen to show Network Proxy Settings dialog. 2. For automatic proxy setup: Enable Automatically detect settings option to use Web Proxy Auto-Discovery Protocol (WPAD), or enable Use setup script option and insert network address of script into Script address box. 3. For manual proxy setup: Enable Use a proxy server option, enter specific IP address and port in Proxy Server Address and Proxy Server Port fields. 4. For addresses not to use proxy server, enter web or IP addresses separated with semicolon (;) in Proxy Server Exceptions field. 5. Enable Not use for local addresses option to bypass proxy server for local network or intranet. 6. Click OK to save and apply network proxy settings or click Cancel to ignore recent changes.

body: 1. Press Utility > Config on the Touch panel and log on as administrator. 2. Select the Connectivity category and Dataflow subgroup. The Dataflow sheet is displayed. 3. Select a DICOM Worklist dataflow or the Query/Retrieve dataflow. 4. Select the Worklist or Query/Retrieve device and press Properties. • No extra info
• Add visible patient info in the DICOM images: displays patient information (name, date of birth and ID) on DICOM images.
• Add title bar: adds the Title bar to the DICOM images. Must be enabled in order for images from the 4D Auto AVQ tool to contain traces, bullseye, 3D model and measurements as part of the stored DICOM Multiframe/Singleframe files when using a dataflow with RAW data disabled.

title: Dataflow concept description
body: Communication between the Vivid Explorer/Vivid Advanced/Vivid Focus ultrasound system and other information providers on the network takes the form of dataflows. Each dataflow defines the transfer of patient information and images from an input source to the system, and from the system to one or several output sources. A dataflow is a set of pre-configured settings. Selecting a dataflow will automatically customize the system to work according to the settings associated with this dataflow.

title: CD and DVD handling recommendation
body: To avoid data loss, never touch the recordable surface of a disk. Handle the disk only by the outer edge. Do not place it face down on a hard surface. Fingerprints or scratches will make the disk unusable. Before usage, verify that the disk surface has no visible scratches. If there are any scratches, do NOT use the disk.

title: Formatting removable media
body: 1. Insert the media in the drive. 2. Press Utility > Config on the Touch Panel. 3. If required, log on to the system. 4. Select the category Connectivity and select the sheet Tools. 5. Select the removable media from the Media drop-down menu (CD-R, DVD-R or USB device). Select Refresh if the media does not appear on the list. 6. Enter a name for the removable media in the Label field. Only the following characters and signs can be used when labeling a media: A - Z, a - z, 0 - 9, "_" and "-". Do not use more than 11 characters or signs. Do not use space. 7. Select Format. A confirmation window is displayed. CAUTION: The formatting process will erase any data present on the media. 8. Select OK to continue. 9. Wait for the display of the Information window indicating that the formatting process is completed. 10. Select OK.

NTP server: Enter URL for time synchronization source. Press Apply to validate the connection. Default server: time.windows.com. 3. Press the Synchronize button to synchronize immediately with selected time source. Button indicates: synchronization in progress, synchronization succeeded, or synchronization failed. 4. Last successful sync. displays the date, time & source of the last successful time synchronization. NOTE: If the time and date is more than 24 hours off when enabling time synchronization, the synchronization might fail. To avoid this, adjust the date and time manually before enabling time synchronization.

title: Battery charge levels for shipping and long-term storage
body: Prior to shipping, the absolute charge level of the system battery must be less than 30%. Prior to long-term storage, the absolute charge level of the system battery must be between 25% and 30%. When Shipping / storage charging mode is selected, the battery will not charge above 28%. Charging stops when the charge level reaches 28%, which is appropriate for shipping or long-term storage.

title: Prepare system battery for shipping or long-term storage
body: 1. Make sure the system is powered with AC. 2. Navigate to Config > System > Battery. 3. Select Shipping / storage charging mode. 4. Disconnect the AC cable and let the battery discharge until shutdown. 5. Reconnect the AC cable and let it charge to above 25%, if it is below that level. Charging stops when the charge level reaches 28%, which is appropriate for shipping or long-term storage.

title: Backup Procedure
body: 1. Press Patient. 2. In the Archive screen, select the dataflow Local Archive - Int. HD. 3. Press Utility > Config on the Touch panel. 4. Select the category Admin. 5. Select the Backup sheet. 6. In the Backup sheet, select as needed: Patient archive to backup the patient records, or System configuration to copy system settings and user presets. 7. Select a removable media or a shared network folder as destination. 8. If the backup is done to a removable media, insert a dedicated media in the drive. 9. Select Start backup. 10. During backup, progress windows are displayed showing the current operation being performed. 11. At the end of the process, the Backup completed window is displayed. Select OK. 12. Make sure to physically label the media. An identification of the system should also be noted on the media and a backup log should be kept.
anchor: Press Patient. 2.  In the Archive screen, select the dataflow Local Archive - Int. HD.

body: 1. Press Utility > Config from the Touch panel. 2. Select the category Admin. 3. Select the Restore sheet. 4. In the Restore sheet, select as needed: Patient archive to restore the patient archive, or System configuration to restore all system settings and user presets, or One or several system configuration items to restore parts of the system settings and user presets. 5. If restore is done from a backup on a removable media, insert the media in the drive. Make sure that Restore from Source Device is selected. 6. Select the appropriate Source device. 7. Select Restore now. 8. Ensure that the correct source is selected and select OK. The selected items are copied to the systems. 9. If connectivity configuration settings are restored, select OK in the information window. 10. Select OK to shut down the system. 11. Restart the system.

product_system: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus
title: Software Download and Installation via Insite RSvP
body: 1. Log on as ADM. 2. Ensure Agent Configuration is correctly configured. 3. Press the Download button at the bottom of the display screen. 4. Available software updates are displayed in list. Press Refresh if needed to query for available updates. 5. Confirm refresh by pressing Yes. 6. Wait for refreshed list to be queried. 7. Select desired software and press Download, or press Close to exit. 8. During download, Status displays as Downloading. Press Pause to suspend or Cancel to exit. Press Resume to continue if paused, or Retry if error occurs. 9. When download complete, press Install button (only ADM users can install). 10. Log in as administrator if not already done. 11. Press Install button to start installation. 12. Click Yes in popup warning to start. After approximately ten minutes, may need to start system manually by pressing On/Off button. System will reboot several times during installation.
anchor: Please make sure system power plug is connected before you press the Install button to avoid installation failures due to power loss.

2. Power on the Vivid Explorer/Vivid Advanced/Vivid Focus and wait for the dialog.
3. Select Install SW … Select OK to proceed with installation or Cancel to cancel installation.
4. Select the file in the list and click Install. Installation commences. The progress bar will fill up multiple times and the system will automatically restart multiple times.
5. Remove the USB stick and press OK to continue the installation.

anchor: Power down the Vivid Explorer/Vivid Advanced/Vivid Focus and insert the USB Flash Drive with the software into one of the USB ports on the ultrasound system.

title: Reload Software on Vivid Explorer/Advanced/Focus
body: 1. Log on as ADM. 2. Select About > System Version. 3. Select Reload Software. 4. In pop-up, select Reload (current software) or Rollback (previous software). For OS Patch: Patch option checked = reload patch only; uncheck Patch to reload full software. 5. If DICOM TLS certificates and WPA-Enterprise configuration recorded and system can stay connected to mains power for duration of software loading (50 to 60 minutes), click OK (else Cancel). 6. System starts software loading and automatically powers down. Wait ten seconds, press ON switch on Operator Panel to restart. System prepares C: drive and loads selected software. 7. System restarts several times during installation (50 - 60 minutes total). 8. Manually restore DICOM TLS certificates and WPA-Enterprise configuration. 9. Power down ultrasound system.

title: Alt+D log collection procedure
body:
To collect logs if the Ultrasound system malfunctions:
1. Simultaneously press Alt+D keys.
2. Enter System ID serial number.
3. Enter Software version.
4. Enter System date and time of occurrence.
5. Enter Sequence of events leading to issue.
6. Note whether the issue is repeatable.
7. Note Imaging mode, probe, preset/application.
8. Note Media brand, speed, capacity, and type.
9. To include protected information, check Include Protected Information (requires Admin privileges).
10. To include a duration, check Time Duration and select from dropdown.
11. Under Destination, select storage media or Service directory.
12. Click Store button.
anchor: If the Ultrasound system malfunctions, simultaneously press the Alt+D keys.

product_system: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus
title: Capturing Network Logs
body:
To troubleshoot network capture logs:
1. On the Ultrasound system, run the Network Capture utility to generate .etl and .cab files for analysis.
2. Locate the .etl file at D:\Service.
3. Transfer these files to a laptop.
4. On the laptop, download Microsoft Message Analyzer (if not already done).
5. In Microsoft Message Analyzer, open the .etl file.
6. To export the .etl file to .cab, select File > Save As and then select Save As or Export.
7. Use Wireshark or some other third-party network sniffer to examine the .cab file.
anchor: Use the Network Capture utility to capture network logs. Once the logs are captured and extracted from the system, use Microsoft Message Analyzer to convert the output, and then Wireshare (or some other network sniffer) to analyze it.

title: Disruptive Mode Operation
body: Disruptive mode is required whenever service performs a function that may disrupt a normal scan. Activating Disruptive mode results in a red message displayed on the task bar. This message indicates that the Ultrasound system needs to be restarted once the service activity is complete. The message remains until the Ultrasound system is restarted. Disruptive mode is required to run diagnostics, clean presets, and reset the patient database, and turn on Virtual Console Observation (VCO). When Disruptive mode is On, all service functionality on the Service desktop is allowed but user operation of the Ultrasound system may be limited. When Disruptive mode is Off, some service functionality on the Service desktop is not available and user operation of the Ultrasound system is normal.

title: Start Virtual Console Observation (VCO)
body:
To start Virtual Console Observation:
1. Navigate to Utilities > Disruptive Mode Utility and set Disruptive mode to On.
2. Navigate to Utilities > Virtual Console Observation.
3. Select Start. When VCO starts, the Windows task bar and Windows desktop display.
4. Modify settings and programs as needed.
5. To stop Virtual Console Observation, click Stop. When VCO is stopped, the Windows desktop is hidden.
6. Restart the Ultrasound system.

title: Change Password
body:
To change the password:
1. Navigate to Utilities > Change Password.
2. Under User Type, select the user.
3. In New Password and Confirm Password, enter the new password.
4. Click Update Password.
5. When a Service User's password has been changed, reboot the Ultrasound system to reflect the password change.

Note: Make sure the Ultrasound system is connected to the network and the agent is configured. The GEService password is used to perform portions of remote service. If the password is changed and the system information is not updated, it may slow down remote service. Both file transfer and SSH depend on the GEService password.

title: Reset Patient Database
body:
To reset the patient database:
1. Back up the patient database.
2. Navigate to Utilities > Disruptive Mode Utility and set Disruptive mode to On.
3. Navigate to Utilities > Reset Patient Database.
4. Click Reset Patient Database.
5. Confirm the patient database has been emptied.

Note: Reset Patient Database deletes the contents of the following folders:
• E:\Scanner\GEMS_IMG
• E:\Scanner\GEMS_REP
This operation automatically shuts down the application before cleaning the patient database. Once the operation is complete, the Ultrasound system reboots with an empty database.

3. Navigate to Utilities > Clean Userdefs.
4. Select the data you want to set to the default settings.

• Connectivity – Deletes this file: %TEST_ROOT%\resources\userdefs\connectivity.res
• Imaging – Deletes this folder: %TEST_ROOT%\resources\userdefs\ImagingPresets\
• Measurement – Delete this folder: %TEST_ROOT%\resources\userdefs\EchoMeasure\

doc_title: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus General Service Manual
product_system: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus
title: Perform network capture
body:
1. Navigate to Utilities > Network Capture.
2. From Network Capture, do the following:
   • Under Maximum Size, select the allowed size of the generated log file.
   • Under Devices, select the DICOM-configured device for which you want to capture information. If no additional devices are configured, only All will be available.
3. Select Start Network Capture to start the process. This causes the network capture to start, enables the Stop button, and updates the Network Capture Status pane and changes the Status to Running.
4. Click the Stop button to end data collection. Stopping is a two-step process:
   • Stops the data collection and immediately closes the .etl file.
   • Collects additional diagnostic data that may help diagnose network issues. When the file is closed, you see "There is no trace session currently in progress". When the remaining data is collected and the .cab file is closed, you are notified in the banner.
anchor: Navigate to Utilities > Network Capture.

title: Battery Safety Warnings
body: Do not disassemble or modify the battery pack. Do not short circuit. Do not keep with metal objects. Never use force to install. Stop using if damaged, emits unusual smell, feels hot, changes color or shape. Only charge in authorized GE HealthCare devices or chargers. Only use GE HealthCare designated battery packs. Store in cool, dry place. Avoid extreme temperatures. Replace battery pack every two years. Remove all rechargeable batteries within 3 years once end of service life notification is received.

body: Before performing any service or removing covers, turn off the system, disconnect the AC power and wait until the power button light turns off (approximately 40 seconds if the system has batteries). doc_title: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus General Service Manual
product_system: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus
title: Battery - Installation Procedure
body: 1. Install the Battery in the reverse order of the removal. 2. Follow installation sequence label on charge box: (1) Press on/off button to turn off system. (2) Disconnect power source. (3)-(4) Press lock lever while pulling out charge box. (5) Push battery box into main frame; latch will lock automatically. (6) Connect power source. (7) Press on/off button to turn on system. 3. Perform Functional Checks. If system fails to start due to incorrect order, disconnect 220V power for ≥60 seconds and reconnect.
anchor: There is a label on the charge box indicating the installation sequence. Please strictly follow the order shown on the label to install the charge box to ensure it functions properly.

product_system: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus
title: Functional Checks for Battery Replacement
body: 1. Check if the Charge Box is fixed securely. 2. Check the battery icon on the status bar of the screen. Ensure that the battery level is displayed correctly. 3. Confirm if the value for battery health status is displayed on Utility page. Go to Utility > Config > About > Battery for checking the battery health status. 4. For those who have purchased the options for 'Transportation Mode' and 'Scanner on Battery', verify that these functions operate correctly.
anchor: After the Battery is installed, please follow the steps below to check whether the Battery is functioning properly.

product_system: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus
title: Charge Box Module Installation
body: 1. Press on/off button to turn off system. 2. Disconnect power source. 3-4. Press down lock lever of rotary push-to-close latch while pulling out charge box. 5. Carefully push battery box into main frame with both hands until latch automatically locks. 6. Connect power source. 7. Press on/off button to turn on system. Note: Follow installation sequence shown on charge box label. If system fails to start, disconnect 220V power for no less than 60 seconds and reconnect.
anchor: Please strictly follow the order shown on the label to install the charge box to ensure it functions properly.

product_system: Vivid Explorer / Vivid Advanced / Vivid Focus
title: General Cleaning - Console and Monitor
body:
1. Console: Use cleaning agent on a soft, non-abrasive, damp cloth to carefully wipe the entire system. Be careful not to get the cloth too wet so that moisture does not enter the console. DO NOT allow any liquid to drip or seep into the system.
2. Monitor + Touch Panel: Clean Monitor surface and Touch Panel with cleaning agent on a soft, non-abrasive, damp cloth. DO NOT spray any liquid directly onto Vivid Explorer/Vivid Advanced/Vivid Focus covers, Monitor, keyboard, etc.
anchor: Use cleaning agent on a soft, non-abrasive, damp cloth to carefully wipe the entire system.

doc_title: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet General Service Manual
product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: Damage in Transportation Procedure
body:
If damage is apparent:
1. Write "Damage in Shipment" on ALL copies of the freight or express bill BEFORE delivery is accepted or "signed for" by a GE HealthCare representative or hospital receiving agent.
2. Report the damage to the carrier.
  • Whether noted or concealed, damage MUST be reported to the carrier immediately upon discovery, or in any event, within 14 days after receipt, and the contents and containers held for inspection by the carrier.
  • A transportation company will not pay a claim for damage if an inspection is not requested within this 14-day period.
anchor: Write "Damage in Shipment" on ALL copies of the freight or express bill BEFORE delivery is accepted or "signed for" by a GE HealthCare representative or hospital receiving agent.

title: Safe Practices - Grounding and Power Requirements
body: To minimize shock hazard, the equipment chassis must be connected to an electrical ground. The ultrasound system is equipped with a three-conductor AC power cable which must be plugged into an approved electrical outlet with safety ground. The power outlet used for this equipment should not be shared with other types of equipment. Both the ultrasound system power cable and the power connector must meet international electrical standards. Connecting the ultrasound system to the wrong voltage level will most likely destroy it.
anchor: To minimize shock hazard, the equipment chassis must be connected to an electrical ground.

title: Wheel and Brake Safety Precautions
body: The ultrasound system is driven by four free-swivel wheels, controlled by black brake pedals situated above the wheel. Examine the wheels frequently for defects to avoid breaking or jamming. Do not move the system when the brakes are engaged. CAUTION: Always place the system on horizontal ground and engage the caster brakes. Always ensure complete brake engagement on all 4 casters by firmly stepping on the brake pedals of the casters. Failure to follow these precautions could result in injury, uncontrolled motion and damage.

title: Charge box assembly and disassembly procedure
body: 1. Press on/off button on the ultrasound system to turn off the system. 2. Disconnect the power source to the ultrasound system. 3. Use one hand to press down the lock lever of the rotary push-to-close latch while at the same time use the other hand to pull out the charge box. 4. Carefully push battery box into main frame with both hands. When the Charge Box is fully installed on the system, the latch will automatically lock. 5. Connect the power source to the ultrasound system. 6. Press on/off button on the ultrasound system to turn on the system.

doc_title: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet General Service Manual
product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: Contact Information to Collect Before Calling Customer Support
body:
Before calling customer support, collect the following information and acquire image (Alt+D) to send to the Customer Care team:
1. Ultrasound system ID serial number.
2. Software version.
3. Date and time of occurrence.
4. Sequence of events leading to issue.
5. Is the issue repeatable?
6. Imaging mode, probe, preset/application.
7. Media brand, speed, capacity, type.
8. Save secondary image capture, cine loop, 4D multi-volume loop.
9. Detailed description of any problem encountered.
10. Where applicable, save the appropriate log files.
Remember to save the log files for each day on a separate media, labelled accordingly. Restart the application before resuming clinical scanning.
anchor: Before you call, identify the following information and acquire image (Alt+D) to send to the Customer Care team:

External peripheral equipment not verified by GE Healthcare must comply with related IEC/EN standards (eg. 60601/62368 series). title: Electrical leakage limits for commercial devices
body: Commercial devices such as laser cameras, printers, VCRs and external monitors usually exceed allowable leakage current limits per IEC/EN60601-1. When plugged into separate AC outlets, they are in violation of patient safety standards. Suitable electrical isolation of external AC outlets or providing the device with extra protective earth is required to meet IEC/EN60601-1 Clause 16 standards for electrical leakage currents.

title: External device connection compliance
body: DANGER: External devices not verified by GE HealthCare can be used only if in compliance with related IEC or ISO Safety standards (eg. 60601/62368 series). Conformance to IEC/EN60601-1 Clause 16 requirements for the whole system must be verified. Accessory equipment connected to analog and digital interfaces must be certified according to respective IEC or ISO Safety standards (e.g. IEC/EN62368-1 for data processing equipment or IEC/EN60601-1 for medical equipment). Anybody connecting additional equipment to signal input/output part configures a medical electrical system and is responsible that the system complies with IEC/EN60601-1 Clause 16.

product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: General Precautions for Installing Alternate On-Board Device
body: 1. The added device must have appropriate safety standard conformance and CE Marking. 2. The total power consumption of the added devices, which connect to the ultrasound system and are used simultaneously, must be less than or equal to the rated supply of the ultrasound system. 3. There must be adequate heat dissipation and ventilation to prevent overheating of the device. 4. There must be adequate mechanical mounting of the device and stability of the combination. 5. Risk and leakage current of the combination must comply with IEC/EN 60601-1. 6. Electromagnetic emissions and immunity of the combination must conform to IEC/EN 60601-1-2.

title: Acclimation time after transport
body: Following transport, allow the system to acclimate before switching it on. Acclimation will take one hour for each 2.5 °C increment when the system's temperature is below 10 °C or above 35 °C. Examples: -20 °C (-4 °F): 12 hours; 10 °C (50 °F) or 35 °C (95 °F): 0 hours; 60 °C (140 °F): 10 hours.

product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: Power ON/Boot Up
body: Step 1: If not already done, connect the mains power cable to the back of the system, then pull down the pull-out protection for power cable. Step 2: Connect the mains power cable to a hospital grade power outlet with the proper rated voltage. Never use an adapter that would defeat the safety ground. Step 3: Switch ON the Circuit Breaker at the rear of the system. Step 4: Press the button on the control console for ~3 seconds. The system starts and performs an initialization sequence. Total time used for start-up is about 2 minutes.
anchor: Connect the mains power cable to a hospital grade power outlet with the proper rated voltage. Never use an adapter that would defeat the safety ground.

title: Troubleshooting LED3 (CPU POST OK) on TMBE board
body:
LED3 indicates CPU BIOS post ok on TMBE board. If LED3 does not light on after LED2 is lighted (normally several seconds):
1. Mostly CPU part of TMBE do not work, consider replacing TMBE board first.
2. Also consider LED4 together; sometimes TMX board defect (such as PCIE hung) may also cause CPU cannot boot up normally.
anchor: If LED3 does not light on after LED2 is lighted (normally several seconds), mostly CPU part of TMBE do not work, consider replacing TMBE board first.

doc_title: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet General Service Manual
product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: Troubleshooting LED4 (MST PWR OK) on TMX board
body:
LED4 indicates MSP MCU, DSP, FPGA power up is ok on TMX board. If LED4 does not light on after LED2 is lighted (normally several seconds):
1. Mostly TMX board need replacement.
2. Try install newest software (with VividFirmwareUpdater) first before replacing TMX; some failures may be caused by firmware and software miss match, which can be fixed by software reloading.
Possible causes:
- Hardware issues, such as a faulty TMX board that may require replacement.
- Firmware issues, which may be resolved by reloading or reinstalling the software using the VividFirmwareUpdater built into the SW.
- Software issues, or an unexpected power loss during a firmware upgrade, can be repaired by reloading or reinstalling the software using the VividFirmwareUpdater built into the SW.
anchor: If LED4 does not light on after LED2 is lighted (normally several seconds), mostly TMX board need replacement.

body:

2. Enter the specific IP address in the Proxy Server Address field.
3. Enter the port in the Proxy Server Port field.
4. For addresses you do not want the system to use the proxy server on, enter web or IP addresses separated with a semicolon (;) in the Proxy Server Exceptions field.
5. Enable the Not use for local addresses option to bypass the proxy server when connecting to local network or intranet resources.
6. Click OK to save and apply network proxy settings or click Cancel to ignore the recent changes.

title: Configure Wireless Network Adapter
body:
1. From the default ultrasound system screen, press Config and log on as ADM.
2. Select Connectivity (lower part of window).
3. Select the Network tab.
4. Click the Configuration button in the lower right corner.
5. Either double-click or select the network you want to connect to, and press the Connect button.
6. If this is the first time you attempt to connect to the network, press OK in the dialog window that appears.
7. In the Network Settings Window, select check-boxes according to preference. If the Connect automatically when this network is in range setting is selected, then this network will auto-connect when available.
8. Set up the security options in the Security tab of connection setup dialog.
9. For WPA/SWPA2 Enterprise with customer-specific certificate, install the certificate using the certificate dialog available from the LDAP config page in Connectivity — Security section or from Connectivity — Network section.
10. After you have finished setting up your connection, press OK. The ultrasound system will then try to establish a connection to your network.
11. Once a connection has been established you will see the status Connected in the Wireless Settings page, next to the network you have connected to.

title: DICOM job status codes
body:
Pending: the job is complete, waiting to be active.
Hold: the job is complete, but suspended, waiting for an action from the user.
Append: the job is incomplete, waiting for more images (Direct store function).
Active: the job is complete and connected to the destination device.
Failed: the job is complete but one or more images failed to transmit to the destination device.
Done: the job is saved to the destination device. The jobs that are done are removed from the spooler after a few minutes.
anchor: Pending: the job is complete, waiting to be active. • Hold: the job is complete, but suspended, waiting for an action from the user.

From DICOM images the user can select between: No extra info; Add visible patient info in the DICOM images (displays patient information name, date of birth and ID on DICOM images); Add title bar (adds the Title bar to the DICOM images, must be enabled in order for images from the 4D Auto AVQ tool to contain traces, bullseye, 3D model and measurements as part of stored DICOM Multiframe/Singleframe files when using a dataflow with RAW data disabled).
4. Enable Use high DICOM resolution if needed (DICOM images stored using higher pixel density; doubles file size when using standard compression settings).
5. Select Color management gamma settings for optimized representation on DICOM workstations.
6. Select Sector size (three different sizes of 2D sector for viewing on DICOM work stations).

title: Adjust dataflow settings
body:
To adjust dataflow settings:
1. Press Utility > Config on the Touch panel and log on as administrator if required.
2. Select the Connectivity category and Dataflow subgroup. The Dataflow sheet is displayed.
3. Select Add Dataflow (choose a custom or factory template).
4. Click on the Edit button on the selected dataflow.
5. Check Default dataflow to make it default (will show at top of dataflow list with star icon).
6. Configure Search as you type (narrows displayed patients as letters/numbers entered).
7. Configure Show today's exam by default (limits displayed patients when box is checked).
8. Configure Send images (Images can be sent immediately after Image Store or at end of exam).
9. If dataflow only for transfer purposes and not for acquiring exams, check the Use for transfer purpose only checkbox.

Note: CD/DVD do not need to be formatted. 2. Press Start. The Disk management processing files window is displayed showing progression of the process. 3. If more than one media is necessary, a dialogue window is displayed asking the user to insert a new media. Press OK after the new media is inserted. 4. When all the files are copied, the Disk management completed window is displayed. 5. Make sure all media are physically labeled according to the list displayed in the Disk management completed window. The media label should also have an identification of the system the Disk management was run from. 6. Press Finish to complete the Disk management operation and file the media.

body: User groups with rights: Admin (all rights), Cardiologist (Create, Delete, Diagnose, activated with Dongle), Fellow (Create, Delete, activated with Dongle), Operator (activated with Dongle), RemoteUsr (ReceiveStreaming, RemoteControl), ConsultingPhys (Diagnose), GEAdmin (Admin, Service, SecureWipe, RemoteControl), Physician (Create, Delete), Sonographer (Create, Delete), DiagPhys (Diagnose), HospAdmin (Create, Delete, Admin), RefDoc (none), SysAdmin (Create, Delete, PresetAdmin, Admin). Rights definitions: Create - Create and update patient record, examination, user and referring members. Delete - Delete patient record, examination, user and referring members. Diagnose - Make the Diagnosing physician/veterinarian available, sign off report. Preset admin - Make application presets protected, delete protected application presets. Print report - Print a report. Admin - System administration. Receive streaming - Allow receiving Vivid images on remote client. Service - Access to service platform. Secure Wipe - Access to erasing patients securely.

product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: Data Backup Procedure
body:
1. Press Patient.
2. In the Archive screen, select the dataflow Local Archive - Int. HD.
3. Press Utility > Config on the Touch panel.
4. Select the category Admin.
5. Select the Backup sheet.
6. In the Backup sheet, select as needed: Patient archive to backup the patient records; System configuration to copy system settings and user presets.
7. Select a removable media or a shared network folder as destination.
8. If the backup is done to a removable media, insert a dedicated media in the drive.
9. Select Start backup.
10. During backup, progress windows are displayed showing the current operation being performed.
11. At the end of the process, the Backup completed window is displayed. Select OK.
12. Make sure to physically label the media. An identification of the system should also be noted on the media and a backup log should be kept.
anchor: In the Archive screen, select the dataflow Local Archive - Int. HD.

body: 1. Log on to the portal website: https://gehealthcare.flexnetoperations.com/flexnet/operationsportal. 2. Log in using the user name (email) and password. 3. body: 1. Power down the Vivid Explorer Vet/Vivid Focus Vet and insert the USB Flash Drive with the software into one of the USB ports on the ultrasound system. Ensure that the system is USB Device Enabled (check Config->Service page). 2. Power on the Vivid Explorer Vet/Vivid Focus Vet and wait for the dialog. 3. Select Install SW … Select OK to proceed with installation or Cancel to cancel installation. 4. Select the file in the list and click Install. Installation commences. The progress bar will fill up multiple times and the system will automatically restart multiple times. Do not power off the system during the software installation. 5. Remove the USB stick and press OK to continue the installation.

product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: Reload software
body: Before starting, record DICOM TLS certificates and WPA-Enterprise configuration. 1. Log on as ADM. 2. Select About > System Version. 3. Select Reload Software. 4. In pop-up, select to reinstall current installed software (Reload) or select previous installed software (Rollback). After installation of an OS Patch, patch software becomes available. The Patch option is checked by default. To reload the full software, uncheck Patch. 5. If you have recorded DICOM TLS certificates and WPA-Enterprise configuration and you are sure the system can stay connected to mains power for the duration of the software loading (50 to 60 minutes), click OK. After clicking OK, the system starts the software loading. The system will automatically power down. Wait ten seconds, then press the ON switch on the Operator Panel to restart. The system will restart several times during the installation process without any user actions, and the software loading will complete in 50 - 60 minutes. 6. Manually restore the DICOM TLS certificates and the WPA-Enterprise configuration that you recorded earlier. 7. Power down the ultrasound system.
anchor: the software loading will complete in 50 - 60 minutes.

title: Capturing Network Logs
body:
1. On the Ultrasound system, run the Network Capture utility to generate .etl and .cab files for analysis.
2. Locate the .etl file at D:\Service.
3. Transfer these files to a laptop.
4. On the laptop, download Microsoft Message Analyzer (if not already done).
5. In Microsoft Message Analyzer, open the .etl file. If DICOM connection is encrypted, you will not be able to see packet contents.
6. To export the .etl file to .cab, select File > Save As and then select Save As or Export.
7. Use Wireshark or some other third-party network sniffer to examine the .cab file.
anchor: Locate the .etl file at D:\Service.

product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: Disruptive Mode Operation
body:
Disruptive mode controls interruptions to Ultrasound system operation. Required for functions that may disrupt normal scan. Activating results in red message on task bar indicating system needs restart once service activity complete. Message remains until system restarted. Prevents patient scanning while system not at optimal status.
Disruptive mode required to: run diagnostics, clean presets, reset patient database, turn on Virtual Console Observation (VCO).
When Disruptive mode On: All service functionality allowed but user operation may be limited.
When Disruptive mode Off: Some service functionality not available, user operation normal.
Local user can set Disruptive mode or allow remote user request (must have Authorize Remote Service Access).
Remote user cannot automatically switch Disruptive mode On; logged in local user must grant access.
anchor: Disruptive mode is required to run diagnostics, clean presets, and reset the patient database, and turn on Virtual Console Observation (VCO).

doc_title: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet General Service Manual
product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: Perform network capture
body:
1. Navigate to Utilities > Network Capture.
2. From Network Capture, do the following:
   • Under Maximum Size, select the allowed size of the generated log file.
   • Under Devices, select the DICOM-configured device for which you want to capture information. If no additional devices are configured, only All will be available.
3. Select Start Network Capture to start the process. This causes the network capture to start, enables the Stop button, and updates the Network Capture Status pane and changes the Status to Running.
4. Click the Stop button to end data collection. Stopping is a two-step process:
   • Stops the data collection and immediately closes the .etl file.
   • Collects additional diagnostic data that may help diagnose network issues. When the file is closed, you see "There is no trace session currently in progress". When the remaining data is collected and the .cab file is closed, you are notified in the banner.
anchor: Under Maximum Size, select the allowed size of the generated log file.

doc_title: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet General Service Manual
product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: Battery Pack Safety Instructions
body: Do not disassemble or modify battery pack. Do not short circuit. Do not keep with metal objects. Never use force to install. Stop using immediately if damaged. Discontinue use if battery emits unusual smell, feels hot, changes color/shape, or appears abnormal. Charge battery as soon as possible after full discharge. Only charge in authorized GE HealthCare devices or chargers, never use third-party charger. Only use GE HealthCare designated battery packs. Store in cool, dry place, never in extreme temperatures. Avoid unattended charging near flammable objects. Replace battery pack every two years for optimal safety and functionality. Once end of service life notification received, remove all rechargeable batteries within 3 years and do not install new battery.
anchor: The battery pack shall be replaced every two years for optimal safety and functionality of the system.

title: Battery Scan Mode Operation
body: On system with fully charged battery, if AC power is lost (voluntary or accidental), system remains in same state and continues working until battery level drops to Empty range. This requires 'Battery scan mode' option enabled. Without 'Battery scan mode' enabled, system supports maximum 5 minutes scanning; after 5 minutes, dialog offers user to switch to Transportation mode or shut down, with no possibility to return to scan mode until AC power is restored.

product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: Service Safety - Electrical Hazard and Power Down Requirements
body: Dangerous voltages capable of causing death are present. Before performing any service or removing covers, turn off the system, disconnect the AC power and wait until the power button light turns off (approximately 40 seconds if the system has batteries). Do not press the power button during service. Remove the batteries before performing service.

title: Service Safety - Heat Hazard and PPE
body: If covers are removed from an operating system, some metal surfaces may be warm enough to pose a potential heat hazard if touched, even while in shutdown mode. Use all Personal Protection Equipment (PPE) such as gloves, safety shoes, safety glasses, and kneeling pads to reduce the risk of injury.

body: 1. Check if the Charge Box is fixed securely. 2. Check the battery icon on the status bar of the screen. Ensure that the battery level is displayed correctly. 3. For those who have purchased the options for 'Transportation Mode' and 'Scanner on Battery', verify that these functions operate correctly.

product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: Charge Box Module - Installation Procedure
body: 1. Install the Charge Box Module in reverse order of removal. Note: Follow the installation sequence label on the charge box strictly. 2. (1) Press on/off button to turn off the system. 3. (2) Disconnect power source. 4. (3)~(4) Use one hand to press down the lock lever of the rotary push-to-close latch while using the other hand to pull out the charge box. 5. (5) Carefully push battery box into main frame with both hands. When fully installed, the latch will automatically lock. 6. (6) Connect power source. 7. (7) Press on/off button to turn on system. 8. Perform Functional Checks. Note: If system fails to start due to incorrect battery replacement order, disconnect 220V power for no less than 60 seconds and reconnect. If still cannot start, contact service personnel.
anchor: disconnect the 220V power supply for no less than 60 seconds and then reconnect it.

title: Functional Checks (60 minutes)
body: 1. B Mode - Verify basic B Mode (2D) operation. Check the basic ultrasound system controls that affect this mode of operation. 2. M Mode - Verify basic M Mode operation. Check the basic ultrasound system controls that affect this mode of operation. 3. C Mode - Verify basic CFM Mode (Color Flow Mode) operation. Check the basic ultrasound system controls that affect this mode of operation. 4. PD Mode - Verify basic PD Mode (Power Doppler Mode) operation. Check the basic ultrasound system controls that affect this mode of operation. 5. Doppler Modes - Verify basic Doppler Mode operation (PW and CW if available). Check the basic ultrasound system controls that affect this mode of operation. 6. 3D Mode - Verify basic 3D Mode operation. Check the basic ultrasound system controls that affect this mode of operation. 7. RealTime 4D Mode (optional) - Verify basic RealTime 4D Mode operation. Check the basic ultrasound system controls that affect this mode of operation. 8. *Applicable Software Options - Verify the basic operation of all optional modes. Check the basic system controls that affect each option's operation.
anchor: The functional checks take about 60 minutes to perform.

doc_title: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet General Service Manual
product_system: Vivid Explorer Vet / Vivid Focus Vet
title: Physical Inspection
body: 1. Labeling - Verify that all ultrasound system labeling is present and in readable condition. 2. Covers - verify all covers are secured in place and are properly aligned with other covers. Replace any covers that are damaged. 3. Control Console - Inspect the control console. Record any damaged or missing items. Replace faulty components, as required. 4. Control Console Movement - verify ease of control console movement in all acceptable directions; ensure that it latches in position as required. 5. Control Console Lighting - Check proper operation of all control console. 6. Monitor - Inspect the Display for scratches and bad pixels. Verify proper operation of Contrast and Brightness controls. Confirm that the monitor arm allows swiveling the screen to the left and to the right, folding the screen to the locked position, release and adjustment backwards and forwards, can be adjusted in the up/down positions. 7. Cables and Connectors - Check all internal cable harnesses and connectors for wear and secure connector seating. Pay special attention to foot switch assembly and probe strain or bend reliefs. 8. Shielding & Covers - Check to ensure that all EMI shielding, internal covers, air flow panels and screws are in place. Missing covers and hardware could cause EMI/RFI problems during scanning. 9. Probe Holders - inspect the Probe Holders for cracks or damage. 10. Power and System Status Indicators - Check for proper operation of all Power and System Status Indicators. 11. External I/O - Check all connectors for damage and verify that the labeling is good. 12. Wheels and Brakes - Check all wheels and casters for wear and verify operation of foot brake, to stop the system from moving, and release mechanism. Check all wheel locks and wheel swivel locks for proper operation. 13. Battery - check that the batteries are not damaged, do not leak, do not emit an odor, and are not deformed or discolored. Observe all warnings and cautions for transportation battery handling, recharging, storing, and/or disposal.
anchor: Missing covers and hardware could cause EMI/RFI problems during scanning.

body: If damage is apparent: 1. product_system: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus (R3)
title: Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Procedure
body:
To apply Lockout/Tagout (LOTO):
1. Plan and prepare for shutdown.
2. Shutdown the equipment.
3. Isolate the equipment.
4. Remove/disconnect the battery, if present.
5. Apply Lockout/Tagout Devices.
6. Control all stored and residual energy.
7. Verify isolation.
All potentially hazardous stored or residual energy is relieved.

product_system: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus (R3)
title: Unpacking the Ultrasound System
body: 1. Cut off the packing strap around the crate (hold the strap clasp with one hand when cutting the strap). 2. Remove the top cover. 3. Remove the 3 plastic locks (rotate the inside plastic lock counterclockwise to remove it and then remove the outside lock). 4. Remove the outside shipping box. 5. Remove the barrier bag from the unit (if the system is transported by air, ignore this step). 6. Remove the PE bag only if the system is transported by air (if the system is transported by sea, ignore this step). 7. Remove the clear plastic (wrapped around the ultrasound system) from the unit. 8. Cut the cable ties around the four wheels. 9. Remove the foams beside the monitor and remove any additional packing material surrounding the system. 10. Unlock the wheels, and then 2 people hold the front handle and rear handle to move the whole system on the ground.

title: IP Settings Configuration
body:
To configure IP settings:
1. Type the name of the Ultrasound system in the Computer Name field.
2. In the IP settings section, identify the ultrasound system to the rest of the network by one of the following:
   • Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) can be used provided your network supports the DHCP protocol.
   • Type the IP-Address. In this case, uncheck the "Enable DHCP" box and enter the IP address, Subnet Mask and default Gateway. Contact your network administrator if you are unsure what values to enter.
3. Select the Network Speed.
4. Press Save and restart the system.

body:
To get the Ultrasound System to recognize another Device on the Network:
1. Select Add. The system creates a device called "NewDevice".
2. Change the name to one of your choosing.
3. Enter the IP address of the device.
4. Save your changes and then press Ping. A "Smiley Face" indicates successful communication between your ultrasound system and the device. A "Frown" indicates failed communication. Check the following:
   • Is the device running?
   • Is it connected to the network?
   • Did you enter the right IP address?

title: Sony UP-D898MD Printer Installation
body: Tools: Common Phillips screwdrivers. Manpower: One person 20 minutes + travel. Preparations: 1. Unpack B/W Printer. 2. Ensure no physical damage. 3. Shut down the system and disconnect the power cord. Installation: 1. Put the AC printer shelf on the bottom of the printer, and then screw 4 screws to fix the printer shelf. 2. Remove the body left and right cover. 3. Unscrew 6 screws and remove the body front cover. 4. Cut the 2 cable clips, then connect the USB cable connector and the AC power cable connector. 5. Insert the printer to the system and screw 2 screws to fix the drawer on the system. 6. Remove the printer cover from body front cover. 7. Install the body covers in the reverse order of removal. 8. Power on the system. 9. Press Utility on the Touch Panel. 10. Select Connectivity > Service, add Standard Print. 11. Highlight Standard Print in the Service list. Select the printer from the Printer pull-down Properties menu. Type the printer name in the Name Field. This name is used on the Button screen. Press Save. 12. Select Button. Select the appropriate print key (Print1, Print2...) from the Physical Print Buttons selection. Select the printer from MyComputer column and press >> to move it to the Printflow View column. Press Save.
section: Sony UP-D898MD Printer Installation > Installation Procedure
anchor: Put the AC printer shelf on the bottom of the printer, and then screw 4 screws to fix the printer shelf.

Scan for surrounding devices. Then select the device name of the ultrasound system in your surrounding device list to pair. 5. The Pincode is shown in the dialogue, click Accept to continue. 6. After the system is powered on, check the option status. 6. Configure the user define key in utility. On the screen, the user defined key name will be displayed. 7. This completes the option installation of the ultrasound system. (Installing corresponding hardware is a prerequisite of loading software option successfully.)

product_system: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus (R3)
title: Connect AC Mains Power to Ultrasound System
body: 1. Ensure that the wall outlet is of appropriate type, and that the Circuit Breaker is turned off. 2. Uncoil the power cable, allowing sufficient slack so that the unit can be moved slightly. 3. Verify that the power cable is without any visible scratches or any sign of damage. 4. Verify that the on-site mains voltage is within the limits indicated on the rating label near the Circuit Breaker on the rear of the unit. 5. Connect the Power Cable's female plug to the Power Inlet at the rear of the unit. 6. Lock the plug in position with the Retaining Clamp (ACC Clamp). 7. Verify that the Mains Power Circuit Breaker is in OFF position, if not, switch it OFF. 8. Connect the Power Cable's other end (male plug) to a hospital grade mains power outlet with the proper rated voltage, and the unit is ready for Power ON/Boot Up.
section: Connect AC (mains) Power to the ultrasound system
anchor: Verify that the on-site mains voltage is within the limits indicated on the rating label near the Circuit Breaker on the rear of the unit.

doc_title: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus General Service Manual
product_system: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus (R3)
title: Archiving Images
body: 1. Insert the archive media. 2. To format the archive media, enter Utility > Connectivity > Removable Media. 3. Format the CD. Verify the format if desired. 4. Images will be moved from the hard drive by date. Therefore, the best way is to label media by date. 5. Specify the EZBackup/EZMove setup on Utility > System > Backup/Restore page. Select Move File Older Than in Days if desired. 6. To start the EZBackup/EZMove procedure, go to the Patient menu and select EZBackup/EZMove. The EZBackup/EZMove Wizard starts. 7. Verify the information on the first page of EZBack/EZMove wizard, then select Next. 8. Verify the information on the EZBackup/EZMove Wizard. After you have gathered the media (allow for one extra media, just in case), you are ready to begin the backup. Press Next. 9. A pop-up message appears that provides you with the media label. Label the media, then insert the media. Press OK. a. Ensure that you label the media with not only the volume name indicated on the Insert Media Message, but with the name of the Versana Premier system where this backup/move procedure was done. b. Update the EZBackup/EZMove log with this information the volume information and the location of the media. c. After the backup/move has been completed, file the media. 10. The system will check whether the media is inside the drive. If the media is in the drive, the window automatically disappears when the checking is completed. The EZBackup progress then begins. If the media is not in the drive, a pop-up message appears notifying that there is no media in the drive. Press OK. A pop-up message appears that provides you with the media label. Label the media, then insert the media. Press OK. 11. The status menu appears. When the backup/move has been complete, press Next. 12. When the backup is complete, the completion wizard page appears. Press Finish.
anchor: Images will be moved from the hard drive by date. Therefore, the best way is to label media by date.

title: Clean the trackball
body: 1. Power off the system. 2. Rotate the dust gasket counterclockwise until it can be removed from the keyboard. 3. Separate the trackball and the gasket. Wipe off any oil or dust from the trackball, gasket and the trackball housing using a cleaner or cotton swab. 4. Assemble the trackball and gasket, then put it into the housing and rotate it clockwise until its notches are set in the position.

product_system: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus (R3)
title: Adjust Color Mode controls functional check
body: Adjust the Active mode gain to set the gain in the color flow area. Adjust Scale to the highest setting that provides adequate flow detection. NOTE: The scale value may affect FPS, Low Velocity Reject, and Sample Volume. Adjust Wall Filter to remove low velocity blood flow and tissue movement that reduces image quality. Adjust Sample volume (SV) to a low setting for better flow resolution, or a higher setting to more easily locate disturbed flows. Adjust Frequency to optimize the color flow display. Higher settings improve resolution. Lower settings improve depth penetration and sensitivity. This does not affect the frequency used for 2D and M-Mode. NOTE: Frequency setting may affect FPS, SV and Low Velocity Reject. Adjust PowerOutput to obtain an acceptable image using the lowest setting possible. NOTE: The Power setting affects all other operating modes. Use Invert to reverse the color assignments in the color flow area of the display. Use Threshold to emphasize either the color flow overlay, or the underlying grey scale tissue detail. Use Baseline to emphasize flow either toward or away from the probe. Use Spatial Filter to reduce noise in the color flow area. Spatial Filter smooths the image by averaging collected data along the same horizontal line. An increase of the spatial filter will reduce noise, but this will also reduce the lateral resolution.
section: Color Mode Checks > Adjust the Color Mode controls
anchor: Adjust the Active mode gain to set the gain in the color flow area.

title: Disruptive mode requirements and behavior
body: Disruptive mode is required to run diagnostics, clean presets, and reset the patient database, and turn on Virtual Console Observation (VCO). When Disruptive mode is On, all service functionality on the Service desktop is allowed but user operation of the ultrasound system may be limited. When Disruptive mode is Off, some service functionality on the Service desktop is not available and user operation of the ultrasound system is normal. Activating Disruptive mode results in a red message displayed on the task bar. This message indicates that the ultrasound system needs to be restarted once the service activity is complete.
anchor: Disruptive mode is required to run diagnostics, clean presets, and reset the patient database, and turn on Virtual Console Observation (VCO).

title: Perform Network Capture
body:
To perform a network capture:
1. Navigate to Utility > Service > Utilities > Network Capture.
2. From Network Capture, do the following:
   • Under Maximum Size, select the allowed size of the generated log file.
   • Under Devices, select the DICOM-configured device for which you want to capture information. If no additional devices are configured, only All will be available.
3. Select Start Network Capture to start the process. This causes the network capture to start, enables the Stop button, and updates the Network Capture Status panel and changes the Status to Running.
4. Click the Stop button to end data collection.
anchor: Navigate to Utility > Service > Utilities > Network Capture.

title: Restore SSA Key That Is Not Validating
body:
To restore an SSA key that is not validating:
1. Remove the SSA key from the ultrasound system.
2. If open, close the Service desktop.
3. Restart the ultrasound system.
4. Once the ultrasound system has restarted, plug in the SSA key.
5. Navigate to Utility > Service > Utilities > SSA License.
6. Click Restore SSA.
7. Check to see if the SSA key validates.
anchor: Remove the SSA key from the ultrasound system.

title: Probe Assessment Procedure
body: 1. Place the probe's carrying case on a stable surface and open the case. 2. Carefully remove the probe and unwrap the probe cord. 3. Put the probe in the probe holder. 4. Prior to inserting the probe, ensure that the connector locking handle is positioned to the left. 5. Align the connector with the probe port and carefully push into the left-most probe port. 6. Turn the connector locking handle to the right to secure the probe connector. 7. Carefully position the probe cord so it is free to move and is not resting on the floor. 8. Press Probe button on the control panel and select the first probe from the probe indicators. 9. Enter global service user interface as GE HealthCare service. 10. In the Diags > Run Diags > ProbeAssessment to check the probe. 11. In the Diags > Run Diags > Diags History to check the probe diagnostic results. Note: Reboot the system after the probe assessment. The probe assessment is only available for the probe connected in the first probe port.
anchor: 8. Press Probe button on the control panel and select the first probe from the probe indicators. 9. Enter global service user interface as GE HealthCare service.

title: Recording settings before software loading
body:
1. Record Computer name and Network Speed in Utility > Connectivity > TCP/IP.
2. Record installed option keys in Utility > Admin > System Admin.
3. Insert backup media, go to Utility > System > Backup/Restore > Media to select media.
4. Go to Utility > System > Backup/Restore, select Patient Archive, User Defined Configuration and Service, then select Backup.
5. Select OK to backup when pop-up warning displays. After backup, remove all external USB devices.
6. Go to Utility > System > General, record Preset Region and Language.
7. Press Patient key, select Data Transfer, set task as Export, specify destination.
8. Select Select All, then Transfer to backup all patient information and images.

product_system: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus (R3)
title: Loading System Software with USB memory stick
body: 1. Insert the Upgrade USB memory stick labeled "System & Application Software" to the USB port of the system. 2. Properly turn off the system by momentarily pressing the Power On/Off Switch. Then select Shutdown in the System Exit Window. (If the system does not shutdown normally, hold down the Power On/Off Switch until the light turns off.) 3. Power on the system and it will detect the USB memory stick automatically. 4. Select the option Load the complete disk, Load the bootable C: partition only or Only Reload/Upgrade Application Software on Touch Panel or use Cursor key to select on LCD screen. 5. If Load the complete disk is selected, a confirmation window will pop out, then select Execute by using Touch Panel or Cursor key to continue. If Load the bootable C: partition only or Only Reload/Upgrade Application Software is selected, system will check if current disk is in Suspend status and follow confirmation prompts. 6. System USB memory stick will be loading. Wait for the software installation to complete. Status bar on the screen indicates the progress (about 30 minutes). 7. The system will display upgrading result and shutdown automatically within 30 seconds. Or click the Shutdown in the screen to shut down the system immediately. If the upgrade fails, select Exit to exit the upgrade process, then remove the USB memory stick. Insert the USB memory stick again and repeat the upgrade process from the Step 2. 8. Remove USB memory stick. Then press Power On/Off switch to power on the system.
section: Loading the System Software with USB memory stick
anchor: Insert the Upgrade USB memory stick labeled "System & Application Software" to the USB port of the system.

title: Secure Wipe Procedure
body: 1. Insert the USB memory stick labeled "System & Application Software" to the system. 2. Properly turn off the scanner by momentarily pressing the Power On/Off Switch. In System-Exit window, select Shutdown to shutdown the system. 3. Power on the system. The system will detect the USB memory stick automatically. 4. Select Secure Wipe. Or select Exit to exit the process. 5. The system indicates all data will be erased, select Execute to continue. 6. The process may take twenty minutes or more. 7. The system will shutdown automatically when the wiping progress completes. Note: Before starting, remove all probes and peripherals. Ensure AC adapter is connected during system upgrade. All the patient data cannot be recovered after wipe process. As the SSD is empty after secure wipe, the system cannot boot up. The software should be loaded first after the wipe process.
