title: Configuration Restore - Restore User Defined Configuration
body:
If Load the complete disk is selected for software upgrade, restore Patient Archive and System Configurations:
1. When system is powered on, go to Utility > Connectivity > TCP/IP to check Computer Name and Network Speed, change if needed. Select Save, then Restart later.
2. Insert backup media.
3. Select System, then select Backup/Restore.
4. In Media field, select the media.
5. To restore all user defined configuration: In Restore field, select User Defined Configuration, then select Restore button. To restore specific items: In Detailed Restore of User Defined field, select items to restore, then select Restore button.
6. After restoring User Defined Configuration, System will restart.
7. After system powered on, go to Utility > System > Backup/Restore. Select Patient Archive, User Defined Configuration and Service under Restore field. Select Restore.
8. Press Patient key on control panel, select Data Transfer. Select task as Import and select source.
9. Select Select All, then select Transfer to restore all patient information and images.
10. Select YesToAll to continue overwrite.

doc_title: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus General Service Manual
product_system: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus (R3)
title: Software download and installation via Insite RSvP
body: 1. Press the notification icon to display the service menu, click Download to check the update. 2. Available software updates are displayed in the list. If you want to refresh the query for available updates, press Refresh. 3. Select the desired software version and press Download to download the software package, or press Exit to exit the window. 4. During the software download process, the status will be displayed as "Downloading". You can press Pause to suspend the download or press Cancel to abort the download. 5. When the download process finishes, the software is ready to be installed in the ultrasound system. Log in with the ADM account, then click Yes to start the installation. 6. The system will reboot several times to complete the installation. 7. After software installation is complete and the system is rebooted, a Reminder after Installation window will appear. This is to remind the user to manually restore configurations if the system has related settings backed up before the software update. 8. Click OK to confirm the installation is completed.
anchor: Press the notification icon to display the service menu, click Download to check the update.

Log in using the user name (e-mail) and password. 3. The License & Delivery Portal dashboard is displayed. All downloadable packages will be listed in a link under Your Downloads. 4. Click the link to enter the Download Packages page. Downloadable packages with links will be listed. Click on the desired link to enter the Downloads page. 5. Right click on the link under File Name, select Save link as... to download the file to your storage device (a readable and writeable USB flash drive with enough capacity).

title: Loading software via End-User Portal
body: 1. Power off the ultrasound system. 2. Insert the USB Flash Drive into a USB port. Ensure that the system is USB Device Enabled. 3. Power on the ultrasound system. The software program files will be recognized automatically, select Install SW... on the Start Application screen. 4. Click OK on StartLoader screen. Then select the package you want to install, and click INSTALL to start installation. 5. When the installation is complete, the system will reboot automatically. 6. Remove the USB stick from the ultrasound device. 7. The whole installation is completed once system reboots.
anchor: Power off the ultrasound system. 2.  Insert the USB Flash Drive into a USB port.

title: Customer Care Schedule - Maintenance task intervals
body: Maintenance task schedule for Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus (assumes average patient load of 15 per day, not primary mobile use). Daily: Clean Probes (or before each use). Weekly: Inspect AC Mains Cable, Inspect Cables and Connectors, Clean Console, Clean Monitor, Clean Filters. Per Facilities QA Program: Console Leakage Current Checks (Twice Annually), Peripheral Leakage Current Checks (Twice Annually), Surface Probe Leakage Current Checks (Twice Annually), Endocavity Probe Leakage Current Checks (Quarterly Annually), Surgical Probe Leakage Current Checks (Quarterly Annually), Measurement Accuracy Checks (Twice Annually), Functional Checks (also after corrective maintenance). NOTE: Maintenance is not mandatory; table is for reference only. Maintenance may require specialized equipment. If usage exceeds typical patient load, increase maintenance frequencies.
section: Maintenance task schedule / How often should maintenance tasks be performed?
anchor: The service procedures and recommended intervals shown in the Care and Maintenance Task Schedule assumes that you use your ultrasound system for an average patient load (15 per day)

doc_title: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus General Service Manual
product_system: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus (R3)
title: System Preliminary Checks
body:
Preliminary checks take about 15 minutes.
1. Ask and Listen - Ask the customer if they have any problems or questions about the equipment.
2. Paperwork - Fill in the top of Ultrasound Inspection Certificate. Record all probes and Ultrasound system options.
3. Power up - Turn the Ultrasound system power on and verify that all fans and peripherals turn on. Watch the displays during power up to verify that no warning or error messages are displayed. Where applicable, confirm that the battery is charged. If no AC Input present, use the internal battery.
4. Probes - Verify that the Ultrasound system properly recognizes all probes.
5. Displays - Verify proper display on the monitor.
6. FFA (server) - Where applicable, for Warranty and Contract Customers only: Verify that InSite is functioning properly. Ensure two-way remote communications.
7. Review Error Logs - Where applicable, Error Logs can be reviewed via system diagnostics.
8. Diagnostics - Optional.
9. Presets - Backup all Customer Presets to an appropriate media.
10. Image Archive - Back up the Image Archive onto appropriate media.
anchor: The preliminary checks take about 15 minutes to perform.

body:

1. B-Mode - Verify basic B-Mode (2D) operation. Check the basic Ultrasound system controls that affect this mode of operation.
2. CF-Mode - Verify basic CF-Mode (Color Flow Mode) operation. Check the basic Ultrasound system controls that affect this mode of operation.

product_system: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus (R3)
title: System Functional Checks
body: 1. Doppler Modes: Verify basic Doppler operation (PW and CW if available). Check the basic Ultrasound system controls that affect this mode of operation. 2. M-Mode: Verify basic M-Mode operation. Check the basic Ultrasound system controls that affect this mode of operation. 3. Probe Elements: Perform an Element Test on each probe to verify that all the probe elements and system channels are functional. 4. Applicable Software Options: Verify the basic operation of all optional modes such as Contrast. Check the basic Ultrasound system controls that affect each options operation. 5. Xmit/Recv Elements: Use the Visual Channel Utility on the loop connect to verify that all system xmit/recv channels are functional. 6. Operator Panel test: Perform the Operator Panel Test Procedure. 7. Keyboard: Do the interactive keyboard test. 8. Monitor: Verify basic monitor display functions. 9. Software Menu check: Verify Software Menu display functions. 10. Peripherals: See Peripheral checks. 11. Measurements: In measurement mode, make distance measurement, get result in result window. Verify the distance by graduate rule.
anchor: Verify basic Doppler operation (PW and CW if available). Check the basic Ultrasound system controls that affect this mode of operation.

doc_title: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus General Service Manual
product_system: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus (R3)
title: General Cleaning Procedure
body: 1. Console: Remove the battery. Use a fluid detergent in warm water on a soft, damp cloth to carefully wipe the entire system. Be careful not to get the cloth too wet so that moisture does not enter the console. 2. Probe Holder: Clean probe holders (they may need to be soaked to remove excess gel). 3. Monitor: Use a soft, non-abrasive folder cloth. Gently wipe the monitor face. DO NOT use a glass cleaner that has a hydrocarbon base (such as Benzene, Methy Alcohol or Methy Ethyl Ketone) on monitor with the filter (anti-glare shield). For general cleaning of the system, recommended to use non-abrasive soap and water solution.
anchor: DO NOT use a glass cleaner that has a hydrocarbon base (such as Benzene, Methy Alcohol or Methy Ethyl Ketone) on monitor with the filter (anti-glare shield).

product_system: Versana Premier / Versana Premier Lotus (R3)
title: Physical inspection checks
body: 1. Verify that all Ultrasound system labeling is present and in readable condition. 2. Inspect the exterior for dents, scratches or cracks. 3. Refer to: Mains cable inspection. 4. Check all internal cable harnesses and connectors for wear and secure connector seating. Pay special attention to footswitch assembly and probe strain or bend reliefs. 5. Check to ensure that all EMI shielding, internal covers, air flow panels and screws are in place. 6. Inspect keyboard and control panel. Note any damaged or missing items. 7. Check for proper operation of all operator panel and Freeze Key light. 8. Inspect the monitor Display for scratches and bad pixels. Verify proper operation of Contrast and Brightness controls. 9. Check all connectors for damage. 10. Check for proper operation of all Power and System Status Indicators. 11. Where applicable, check that the battery is not damaged, does not leak, does not emit an odor, and is not deformed or discolored.
anchor: Check all internal cable harnesses and connectors for wear and secure connector seating. Pay special attention to footswitch assembly and probe strain or bend reliefs.

title: Basic probe cleaning
body: 1. Disconnect the probe from the ultrasound console and remove all coupling gel from the probe by wiping with a soft cloth and rinsing with flowing water. 2. Wash the probe with mild soap in lukewarm water. Scrub the probe as needed using a soft sponge, gauze, or cloth to remove all visible residue from the probe surface. Prolonged soaking or scrubbing with a soft bristle brush (such as a toothbrush) may be necessary if material has dried onto the probe surface. 3. Rinse the probe with enough clean potable water to remove all visible soap residue. 4. Air dry or dry with a soft cloth.
anchor: Wash the probe with mild soap in lukewarm water. Scrub the probe as needed using a soft sponge, gauze, or cloth to remove all visible residue from the probe surface.

title: Chassis leakage current test - generic procedure
body: The test verifies the isolation of the power line from the chassis. The testing meter is connected from accessible metal parts of the case to ground. Measurements should be made with the unit ON and OFF, with the power line polarity Normal and Reversed. Record the highest reading of current. When using the Microguard or a similar test instrument, its power plug may be inserted into the wall outlet and the equipment under test is plugged into the receptacle on the panel of the meter. This places the meter in the grounding conductor and the current flowing from the case to ground will be indicated in any of the current ranges. The maximum allowable limit for chassis source leakage is shown in Table 10-13 Chassis Leakage Current Limits - Accessible Metal Surface on page 308.
section: Chassis leakage current test / Generic procedure
anchor: Measurements should be made with the unit ON and OFF, with the power line polarity Normal and Reversed.

title: Probe leakage current test - definition
body: This test measures the current that would flow to ground from any of the probes through a patient who is being scanned and becomes grounded by touching some other grounded surface. Some leakage current is expected on each probe, depending on its design. Small variations in probe leakage currents are normal from probe to probe. Other variations will result from differences in line voltage and test lead placement. It is abnormal if no leakage current is measured. If no leakage current is detected, check the configuration of the test equipment.

1. Write "Damage in Shipment" on ALL copies of the freight or express bill BEFORE delivery is accepted or "signed for" by a GE HealthCare representative or hospital receiving agent.
2. Report the damage to the carrier. Whether noted or concealed, damage MUST be reported to the carrier immediately upon discovery, or in any event, within 14 days after receipt, and the contents and containers held for inspection by the carrier. A transportation company will not pay a claim for damage if an inspection is not requested within this 14-day period.

body: 1. Keep the Ultrasound system at least 5 meters (15 feet) away from other EMI sources. 2. Check grounding of the power cord and power outlet. 3. After repairing or updating, replace all covers and tighten all screws. 4. Any cable with an external connection requires a magnet wrap at each end. 5. Replace Radio Frequency gasket if more than 20% or a pair of the fingers are broken. 6. Never place a label where Radio Frequency gaskets meet the Ultrasound system. 7. Use GE specified harnesses and peripherals. 8. Do not allow cables to lie across the top of the Card Rack or hang out of peripheral bays. Loop excess length inside peripheral bays. Attach monitor cables to the frame.

title: Unpacking the ultrasound system
body:
1. Cut off the packing strap around the crate. Hold the strap clasp with one hand when cutting the strap.
2. Remove the top cover.
3. Remove the 3 plastic locks. Rotate the inside plastic lock counterclockwise to remove it and then remove the outside lock.
4. Remove the outside shipping box.
5. Remove the barrier bag from the unit (if system transported by sea; if by air, ignore this step).
6. Remove the PE bag only if the system is transported by air (if by sea, ignore this step).
7. Remove the clear plastic wrapped around the ultrasound system from the unit.
8. Cut the cable ties around the four wheels.
9. Remove the foams beside the monitor and remove any additional packing material surrounding the system.
10. Unlock the wheels, and then 2 people hold the front handle and rear handle to move the whole system on the ground.

product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: TCP/IP Network Configuration
body:
1. Press Utility on the touch panel and login as admin.
2. Select Connectivity on the screen.
3. Select TCP/IP tab.
4. Type the name of the Ultrasound system in the Computer Name field (no spaces in name).
5. In the IP settings section, identify the ultrasound system to the rest of the network. Do not use Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP). Uncheck the "Enable DHCP" box and enter the IP address, Subnet Mask and default Gateway.
6. Select the Network Speed.
7. Press Save and restart the system.
NOTE: Do not set up the system with DHCP. The IP address MUST BE static for the diagnostic and DICOM to function correctly. The Versana Premier IP address MUST BE unique.
anchor: Do not set up the system with DHCP. The IP address MUST BE static for the diagnostic and DICOM to function correctly

product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: Sony UP-D898MD Printer Installation
body: Tools: Common Phillips screwdrivers. Manpower: One person 20 minutes + travel. Preparations: 1. Unpack B/W Printer. 2. Ensure no physical damage. 3. Shut down the system and disconnect the power cord. Installation: 1. Put the AC printer shelf on the bottom of the printer, and then screw 4 screws to fix the printer shelf. 2. Remove the body left and right cover. 3. Unscrew 6 screws and remove the body front cover. 4. Cut the 2 cable clips, then connect the USB cable connector and the AC power cable connector. 5. Insert the printer to the system and screw 2 screws to fix the drawer on the system. 6. Remove the printer cover from body front cover. 7. Install the body covers in the reverse order of removal. 8. Power on the system. 9. Press Utility on the Touch Panel. 10. Select Connectivity > Service, add Standard Print. 11. Highlight Standard Print in the Service list. Select the printer from the Printer pull-down Properties menu. Type the printer name in the Name Field. This name is used on the Button screen. Press Save.
anchor: One person 20 minutes + travel.

body: 1. Connect the Bluetooth Adapter to the USB port on the ultrasound system. 2. Reboot the system. 3. After the power-up sequence is complete, press Utility on the Control Panel. Select Connectivity > Bluetooth, click Add New Device. For Bluetooth Adapter connection, the operator must login as Administrator. 4. Follow the Bluetooth pairing wizard to turn on Bluetooth on your mobile device. Scan for surrounding devices. Then select the device name of the ultrasound system in your surrounding device list to pair. The ultrasound system does not support to pair with Apple device. 5. The Pincode is shown in the dialogue, click Accept to continue. 6. On your mobile device a dialogue box should appear asking for permission to connect to the ultrasound system. Click PAIR and wait for the process to complete. 7. After pairing is done, the mobile device name appears in the Authorized Bluetooth Devices field.

title: Connect AC (mains) Power to the Ultrasound System
body: 1. Ensure that the wall outlet is of appropriate type, and that the Circuit Breaker is turned off. 2. Uncoil the power cable, allowing sufficient slack so that the unit can be moved slightly. 3. Verify that the power cable is without any visible scratches or any sign of damage. 4. Verify that the on-site mains voltage is within the limits indicated on the rating label near the Circuit Breaker on the rear of the unit. 5. Connect the Power Cable's female plug to the Power Inlet at the rear of the unit. 6. Lock the plug in position with the Retaining Clamp (ACC Clamp). 7. Verify that the Mains Power Circuit Breaker is in OFF position, if not, switch it OFF. 8. Connect the Power Cable's other end (male plug) to a hospital grade mains power outlet with the proper rated voltage, and the unit is ready for Power ON/Boot Up.
section: Power ON/Boot Up > Connect AC (mains) Power to the ultrasound system
anchor: Verify that the on-site mains voltage is within the limits indicated on the rating label near the Circuit Breaker on the rear of the unit.

product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: Switch ON the AC Power to the Ultrasound System
body: 1. Switch ON the Mains Power Circuit Breaker at the rear of the unit. You should hear a "click" from the relays in the AC Power and the unit is ready to boot. 2. Press once on the On/Off key on the Operator Panel to boot the unit. Normal boot sequence: a. Unit's ventilation fan starts on full speed, but slows down after a few seconds. b. Power is distributed to peripherals, Operator Panel (Console), Monitor, Front End Processor and Back End Processor. c. Back End Processor starts and loads software. d. Start Screen is displayed. e. Start-up bar indicating time used for software loading is displayed. f. Software initiates and sets up Front End electronics. g. Backlight in keyboard is lit. h. Either a 2D screen (probe connected) or No Mode screen (no probe) is displayed.
section: Power ON/Boot Up > Switch ON the AC Power to the Ultrasound System

Verify the information on the first page of EZBack/EZMove wizard, then select Next. 8. Verify the information on the EZBackup/EZMove Wizard. Press Next. 9. A pop-up message appears that provides you with the media label. Label the media, then insert the media. Press OK. 10. The system will check whether the media is inside the drive. 11. The status menu appears. When the backup/move has been complete, press Next. 12. When the backup is complete, the completion wizard page appears. Press Finish.

body:

product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: Adjust Color Mode controls
body:
• Adjust the Active mode gain to set the gain in the color flow area.
• Adjust Scale to the highest setting that provides adequate flow detection. Note: The scale value may affect FPS, Low Velocity Reject, and Sample Volume.
• Adjust Wall Filter to remove low velocity blood flow and tissue movement that reduces image quality.
• Adjust Sample volume (SV) to a low setting for better flow resolution, or a higher setting to more easily locate disturbed flows.
• Adjust Frequency to optimize the color flow display. Higher settings improve resolution. Lower settings improve depth penetration and sensitivity. This does not affect the frequency used for 2D and M-Mode. Note: Frequency setting may affect FPS, SV and Low Velocity Reject.
• Adjust PowerOutput to obtain an acceptable image using the lowest setting possible. Note: The Power setting affects all other operating modes.
anchor: Adjust Scale to the highest setting that provides adequate flow detection.

doc_title: Versana Premier Vet General Service Manual
product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: Adjust PW Doppler Mode controls
body: Adjust the Active mode gain to set the gain in the spectral Doppler area. Adjust Wall Filter to reduce unwanted low velocity blood flow and tissue movement. In PW mode, adjust Sample volume to low setting for better resolution, or higher setting to more easily locate the disturbed flows. Adjust the Compression setting to balance the effect of stronger and weaker echoes and obtain the desired intensity display. Adjust Frequency to optimize flow display. Higher setting will improve resolution and the lower setting will increase the depth penetration. Adjust Frame rate to a higher setting to improve motion detection, or to a lower setting to improve resolution. Adjust Power Output to obtain an acceptable image using the lowest setting possible. This is particularly important in CW mode, as the energy duty cycle is 100% (constant). Use the Sweep Speed to optimize the sweep speed. To view signal detail, adjust Scale to enlarge the vertical spectral Doppler trace. Use Invert to reverse the vertical component of the spectral Doppler area of the display. Use Angle Correct to steer the ultrasound beam to the blood flow to be measured.
section: PW Doppler Mode Checks > Adjust the PW Doppler Mode controls
anchor: This is particularly important in CW mode, as the energy duty cycle is 100% (constant).

title: Collect Trouble Image with Logs (Alt+D)
body: Press the Alt+D keys simultaneously. This will collect a screen capture of the image monitor, system presets and several log files in a date and time stamped '.zip' file. When Alt+D is pressed, a menu box appears that allows for: 1. a place to enter a description of the issue; 2. a checkbox to indicate a System lockup; 3. a checkbox to include protected information (requires related privilege); 4. a choice to export a pre-formated CD-R/DVD-R or save to the export directory D: drive (for remote viewing through FFA); 5. Service Log (Power ON/OFF record, system memory monitor record, USB connection record, Network Adapter connection status, etc.); 6. Complete Log (all software logs except service related logs). For troubleshooting, export Complete Log.

product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: Disruptive mode operation
body: Disruptive mode is required whenever service performs a function that may disrupt a normal scan. Activating Disruptive mode results in a red message displayed on the task bar. This message indicates that the ultrasound system needs to be restarted once the service activity is complete. The message remains until the ultrasound system is restarted. Disruptive mode is required to run diagnostics, clean presets, and reset the patient database, and turn on Virtual Console Observation (VCO). When Disruptive mode is On, all service functionality on the Service desktop is allowed but user operation of the ultrasound system may be limited. When Disruptive mode is Off, some service functionality on the Service desktop is not available and user operation of the ultrasound system is normal.
anchor: Disruptive mode is required to run diagnostics, clean presets, and reset the patient database, and turn on Virtual Console Observation (VCO).

title: Remote Access Connection Procedure
body: 1. In the server side, type the CRM No. of the system which the OLE would remotely connect to, and select Get Started. Remote FFA link: https://ffa.health.ge.com/#/di/home. 2. Go to Diags > Run Diags > Diags History to check results. CAUTION: Reboot system after probe assessment. NOTE: Diagnostic result is for reference only, not used to decide probe defect.

doc_title: Versana Premier Vet General Service Manual
product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: Loading System Software with USB Memory Stick
body: 1. Insert the Upgrade USB memory stick labeled "System & Application Software" to the USB port of the system. 2. Properly turn off the system by momentarily pressing the Power On/Off Switch. Then select Shutdown in the System Exit Window. NOTE: If the system does not shutdown normally, hold down the Power On/Off Switch until the light turns off. 3. Power on the system and it will detect the USB memory stick automatically. 4. Select the option Load the complete disk, Load the bootable C: partition only or Only Reload/Upgrade Application Software on Touch Panel or use Cursor key to select on LCD screen. You can also select Exit to exit the upgrade process. 5. If Load the complete disk is selected, a confirmation window will pop out, then select Execute by using Touch Panel or Cursor key to continue. If Load the bootable C: partition only or Only Reload/Upgrade Application Software is selected, system will check if current disk is in Suspend status. If yes, press Execute to continue. If the disk is not in Suspend status, select Shutdown to suspend via Utility > Admin > System Admin > Disk Encryption page, or select Execute to continue (requires recovery key or password later). 6. System USB memory stick will be loading. Wait for the software installation to complete. Status bar on the screen indicates the progress (about 30 minutes). 7. The system will display upgrading result and shutdown automatically within 30 seconds. Or click the Shutdown in the screen to shut down the system immediately. If the upgrade fails, select Exit to exit the upgrade process, then remove the USB memory stick. Insert the USB memory stick again and repeat the upgrade process from Step 2. 8. Remove USB memory stick. Then press Power On/Off switch to power on the system.
section: Loading the System Software with USB memory stick
anchor: Insert the Upgrade USB memory stick labeled "System & Application Software" to the USB port of the system.

body: 1. When the system is powered on, go to Utility > Connectivity > TCP/IP to check if the Computer Name and Network Speed display as desired and change them if needed. 2. Select Save, then select Restart later. 3. Insert the media which is used to back-up. 4. Select System, then select Backup/Restore. 5. In the Media field, select the media. 6. In the Restore field, select User Defined Configuration. Then select Restore button in the Restore field. 7. Select OK to continue when Warning message displays. 8. After restoring the User Defined Configuration, the System will restart.
anchor: If the user would restore all user defined configuration, in the Restore field, select User Defined Configuration.Then select Restore button in the Restore field.

doc_title: Versana Premier Vet General Service Manual
product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: Configuration Restore - Restore Selected Items from Detailed User Defined
body: 1. After inserting backup media and navigating to System > Backup/Restore, in the Detailed Restore of User Defined field, select the items the user would like to restore. 2. Then select Restore button in the Detailed Restore of User Defined field. 3. Press OK to continue when pop-up warning messages display. How many warning message windows show up depends on how many items of Detailed Restore of User Defined are selected to restore. 4. After restoring the User Defined Configuration, the System will restart.
anchor: If the user would not restore all user defined configuration, in the Detailed Restore of User Defined field , select the items the user would like to restore.

doc_title: Versana Premier Vet General Service Manual
product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: Restore Patient Archive and Service Data
body: 1. After the system is powered on, go to Utility > System > Backup/Restore. 2. Select Patient Archive, User Defined Configuration and Service under Restore field. 3. Select Restore. 4. Select OK to continue when Warning message displays. 5. Select OK to continue when Question message displays. 6. During the restoring process, a series of pop-up message will display. Press Ok to continue. Note: If the user already restores the detailed User Defined Configuration in previous step, DO NOT select User Defined Configuration in this step. Note: If the user selects Patient Archive, the patient data will be restored but the exam images might be damaged thus unable to read.
anchor: Select Patient Archive, User Defined Configuration and Service under Restore field.

doc_title: Versana Premier Vet General Service Manual
product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: Software update via Insite RSvP - Download and Installation
body: Requires administrator (ADM) rights. Steps: 1. Press notification icon to display service menu, click Download to check update. 2. Available software updates displayed in list; press Refresh to query updates. 3. Select desired software version and press Download, or press Exit. 4. During download, status shows 'Downloading'; press Pause to suspend or Cancel to abort. 5. When download finishes, login with ADM account, click Yes to start installation. 6. System will reboot several times to complete installation. 7. After installation complete and system rebooted, Reminder after Installation window appears. 8. Click OK to confirm installation completed. Download time: approximately 30 minutes (varies by network speed). Installation time: approximately 30 minutes. End open exams before update. Backup presets and patient data before update.
anchor: Press the notification icon to display the service menu, click Download to check the update.

title: Software update via End-User Portal - Download from Portal
body: For customers with end-user eDelivery option. Steps: 1. Log on to portal website https://gehealthcare.flexnetoperations.com/flexnet/operationsportal (provided via welcome email). 2. Log in using user name (e-mail) and password. 3. License & Delivery Portal dashboard displays; all downloadable packages listed under Your Downloads. 4. Click link to enter Download Packages page; click desired link to enter Downloads page. 5. Right click on link under File Name, select Save link as... to download file to storage device (readable/writeable USB flash drive with enough capacity). 6. Load downloaded software on ultrasound system from selected storage location.

product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: Loading Software from USB Flash Drive
body: Steps: 1. Power off ultrasound system. 2. Insert USB Flash Drive into USB port. 3. Power on ultrasound system; software program files recognized automatically, select Install SW... on Start Application screen. 4. Click OK on StartLoader screen; select package to install and click INSTALL to start. 5. When installation complete, system reboots automatically. 6. Remove USB stick from ultrasound device. 7. Whole installation completed once system reboots. Ensure system is USB Device Enabled. Installation time depends on type of update.
anchor: Power on the ultrasound system. The software program files will be recognized automatically, select Install SW... on the Start Application screen.

product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: Customer Care Schedule - Maintenance Intervals
body:
Recommended maintenance intervals for average patient load (15 per day):
1. Daily: Clean Probes (or before each use)
2. Weekly: Inspect AC Mains Cable, Inspect Cables and Connectors
3. Monthly: Clean Console, Clean Monitor, Clean Filters
4. Per Facilities QA Program: Console Leakage Current Checks (Twice Annually), Peripheral Leakage Current Checks (Twice Annually), Surface Probe Leakage Current Checks (Twice Annually), Endocavity Probe Leakage Current Checks (Quarterly Annually), Surgical Probe Leakage Current Checks (Quarterly Annually), Measurement Accuracy Checks (Twice Annually), Functional Checks (also after corrective maintenance).
Note: System does not have mandatory periodic maintenance inspections. If usage exceeds typical patient load, increase maintenance frequencies. Maintenance may require specialized equipment.

title: System preliminary checks
body: Preliminary checks take about 15 minutes. Steps: 1. Ask customer about problems/questions. 2. Fill in Ultrasound Inspection Certificate top; record all probes and system options. 3. Power up: turn power on, verify fans and peripherals; watch displays for warnings/errors; confirm battery charged if applicable. 4. Verify system recognizes all probes. 5. Verify proper monitor display. 6. For Warranty/Contract customers: verify InSite functioning, ensure two-way remote communications. 7. Review Error Logs via diagnostics. 8. Diagnostics (optional). 9. Backup all Customer Presets to media. 10. Back up Image Archive to media.

doc_title: Versana Premier Vet General Service Manual
product_system: Versana Premier Vet (R3)
title: General cleaning procedure
body: 1. Console: Remove the battery. Use a fluid detergent in warm water on a soft, damp cloth to carefully wipe the entire system. Be careful not to get the cloth too wet so that moisture does not enter the console. 2. Probe Holder: Clean probe holders (they may need to be soaked to remove excess gel). 3. Monitor: Use a soft, non-abrasive folder cloth. Gently wipe the monitor face. DO NOT use a glass cleaner that has a hydrocarbon base (such as Benzene, Methy Alcohol or Methy Ethyl Ketone) on monitor with the filter (anti-glare shield). For general cleaning of the system, we recommended to use non-abrasive soap and water solution.
anchor: DO NOT use a glass cleaner that has a hydrocarbon base (such as Benzene, Methy Alcohol or Methy Ethyl Ketone) on monitor with the filter (anti-glare shield).

Check all internal cable harnesses/connectors for wear, secure seating; pay special attention to footswitch and probe strain/bend reliefs. 5. Check all EMI shielding, internal covers, air flow panels, screws in place. 6. Inspect keyboard/control panel for damage or missing items. 7. Check operator panel and Freeze Key light operation. 8. Inspect monitor for scratches, bad pixels; verify Contrast/Brightness controls; confirm monitor arm allows swivel, folding, adjustment. 9. Check all I/O connectors for damage. 10. Check Power and System Status Indicators operation. 11. Where applicable, check battery not damaged, no leaks, no odor, not deformed/discolored.

title: Basic probe cleaning
body: 1. Disconnect probe from console, remove all coupling gel by wiping with soft cloth and rinsing with flowing water. 2. Wash probe with mild soap in lukewarm water; scrub with soft sponge, gauze or cloth to remove all visible residue. Prolonged soaking or scrubbing with soft bristle brush may be needed if material dried on surface. Do not submerge above strain relief (not sealed). Do not allow fluid into/onto connector. Never use excessive force when cleaning lens face. 3. Rinse probe with enough clean potable water to remove all visible soap residue. 4. Air dry or dry with soft cloth.

As a work around, check the other outlets to see if they could be used instead.
